Screenshot via Reuters Connect / CGTV News. Dr. Darvishi said the layers of trauma created by the school massacre have touched every household in Minab. "The 16 psychologists and experts who were from Minab, all of them said that we cannot provide mental health services because our own loved ones were at the school," she said. "Minab is a city where many are related to one another or there was a neighbor who someone lost, or someone from our own family, and our own thoughts are filled with grief and stress from this issue." The children who survived that day are haunted by guilt and shame, as are many parents of the victims. "In grief, there are several stages. The first stage is denial, the next stage is self-criticism, anger, and depression until the acceptance stage happens. Many parents are at the self-criticism stage, and the feeling of guilt," Darvishi said. "I had a talk with a mother who told me that she was to blame for her child's martyrdom, because 'My son told me that morning that he had a stomach ache and didn't want to go to school. I killed my son. I was the one who caused my son's death.'" Salem said the night of the bombing she was calling as many of the parents of her students as she could, as well as those of her former students. She recalled how the parent of one of her students confronted her. "Didn't you say my child was your child? You saved Yassin. You couldn't save my child?" Salem remembered. "I said, 'I swear he wasn't with me.'" She paused to regain her composure. "It is very hard." The surviving children of Minab have recurring nightmares and many wake up screaming. "Some of them say, 'We hear our friend's voice calling me for help, and I couldn't help him. No matter how much I searched, I couldn't help my friend. I couldn't find him,'" said Darvishi. "Their dreams are mostly explosions, terrible noises, the body parts they saw, the voices of their teachers. They dream that they're at school and it's quiet and then there's an explosion. They dream about what they experienced." Many surviving children lost their appetites, their ability to concentrate or comprehend the time or day. Some believe their friends or teachers may still be alive and ask if they can look for them in the rubble of the school. | | ---|---|--- A drawing by Asra, a child who survived the Minab school bombing. The psychologist treating her said Asra saw the severed hand of a classmate. "I've heard that at the Flowerbed of Martyrs Cemetery, a child came and took matches, took a lighter to burn their own hand and leg to see how the ones who burned felt, what their pain felt like," said Salem. "Imagine a six-year-old child speaking about this, saying, 'I saw a hand. I think it was Ali's hand. I saw a leg. I think it was him.' And they have this feeling that maybe they're not a good person. Children don't have the ability to analyze. Oftentimes, they think maybe they weren't good and that's why they couldn't save their friends," Darvishi said. "They have severe guilt, a severe guilty conscience." Salem said that her 8-year-old niece, who was also a student at the school and survived the bombing, believes the U.S. and Israel are still hunting the surviving students. "She said, 'I swear, they're looking for the children of Shajareh Tayyebeh School. They want to martyr all of us and that's when the war will end.'" "A Phenomenon of Sinister Injustice" On the morning of April 8, 1970, Israeli warplanes crossed into Egyptian airspace and conducted a direct strike on Bahr el-Baqar primary school south of Port Said. It was 9:20 a.m., and there were more than 100 students in the school at the time. The U.S.-manufactured F-4 Phantom II jets dropped five bombs and fired two missiles at the school and unloaded machine gun rounds into the building. The structure was completely flattened, killing at least 34 children and wounding more than four dozen others. It became known in Bahr el-Baqar as "The Black Day." The Israeli attack occurred during a period known as the "war of attrition" that followed the end of the 1967 war. Tel Aviv subsequently claimed that its intelligence had mistakenly determined the school was a military target, but in the immediate aftermath of the strike, Defense Minister Moshe Dayan defended the attack. "We have checked and re-checked and there was no mistake this time," he Israeli radio, saying that he was "convinced beyond any doubt" that the Israeli planes hit a military base and if Israel had bombed a school, it was inside the base. More than a half a century after the Bahr el-Baqar school bombing by Israel, the U.S. has followed a similar narrative trajectory. It is a familiar one: When the U.S. and its allies kill civilians, it is assumed to be unintended, "collateral damage," or the fault of their adversaries who use children as human shields. In April, a group of more than 100 prominent international law experts--including former U.S. military judges advocate general--published an asserting that the Minab strike "likely violates international humanitarian law, and if evidence is found that those responsible were reckless, it could also be a war crime. The strike is among the deadliest single attacks by the U.S. military on civilians in recent decades." | | ---|---|--- Women hold up schoolbooks and a backpack of children killed in the U.S. strike in Minab, on March 3, 2026. Photo by Morteza Akhondi. In September, a UN concluded that the U.S. had committed a war crime in its attack on the school, charging, "when targeting the school building, the U.S. acted willfully, that is with the requisite mental element of recklessness." The mission's report cited "deprioritization of civilian harm mitigation" measures by top U.S. officials and open disregard for international humanitarian law principles. It cited the use of outdated maps as well as publicly available data clearly showing the school was a civilian site prior to the onset of the war. "The U.S.'s failure to update information in relation to the school in its targeting databases and to verify that the building was a military objective before launching the attack went beyond mere negligence," the mission determined. "Rather, the U.S. directed the strikes at the building of the school while being aware of a substantial risk of striking a civilian object and acting recklessly as regards the possibility that this would happen." The mission concluded there are "reasonable grounds to believe the United States committed the war crime of launching indiscriminate attacks resulting in the loss of life or injury to civilians or damage to civilian objects." Iran is weighing its legal options. "We will pursue this. This principle still exists that aggressors shall not go unpunished," said Rahimi, Iran's Justice Minister. In Iran itself, prosecutors and criminal investigators have gathered an enormous volume of forensic materials and eyewitness testimony. They recovered the shrapnel and remnants of the U.S. Tomahawk missiles and guidance systems. Rahimi described the publicly available evidence that this was a direct hit on a clearly identified school as overwhelming and indisputable. The official figure reported by the Ministry of Justice remains 168 people killed in the attacks, but to date only 156 bodies have been identified. "The fear and terror they created--they did this deliberately," Rahimi said. "They wanted to create this fear and panic." He said that Iran is gathering evidence indicating the strike was intentional, though he declined to offer details. | | ---|---|--- The Shajareh Tayyebeh School after the U.S. strike. Photo by Hassan Ghaedi /Anadolu via Getty Images. "The wall paintings that are at the school here make it completely visible that it is a school. The U.S. has used missiles that are equipped with cameras, and some operator directs this missile," he said, referring to the Tomahawks. "This missile, with its camera that's seeing its target, if it becomes aware that this is not the target it wants, it can circle around that target for two hours if it wants to, and not hit it, and change its course." The domestic case has been transferred from Minab to the Tehran prosecutor and a criminal prosecution will be conducted. "At the school in Minab, because a civilian location was hit, in fact, we say that it is a war crime," Rahimi said. After a domestic ruling is issued, Rahimi said, Iran will request that other nations enforce the decision. The Iranian parliament is also in the process of preparing legislation, he said, that would create a framework for Iran to assert international jurisdiction, allowing it to issue arrest warrants. "In the end, this is a phenomenon of sinister injustice that must be atoned for in this world," Rahimi said. "It has become the law of the jungle. How many children were martyred in Gaza?" Rahimi also said Iran will ask countries that have universal jurisdiction laws, which allow nations to prosecute grave crimes even if they did not occur within their boundaries or have any connection to their citizens, to issue indictments. Perhaps the most famous case of a nation using universal jurisdiction happened in 1998, when Spanish judge Baltasar Garzon issued an international arrest warrant for former U.S.-backed Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet. The UK respected the indictment and arrested Pinochet who was receiving medical treatment in London at the time. When Pinochet tried to fight extradition, the House of Lords issued a landmark ruling that a former head of state does not have immunity for crimes such as torture. While many nations do have universal jurisdiction laws on the books that would allow for the issuance of indictments, such an action would be seen as an extraordinary confrontation with the U.S. government. "This path depends mostly on political will," said Brody, the veteran war crimes prosecutor. "A European or other government must be willing to expend diplomatic capital, face U.S. pressure, and commit resources to a prosecution that has no direct connection to its own territory." Askari, the Iranian international law expert, said that while Iran is rightly seeking all avenues for justice, the chances of success through universal jurisdiction are slim. "We have to again be realistic and know that we are talking about the high ranking officials of the U.S. administration," he said. "I do not know a country in the world at the moment that has a good diplomatic relationship with the Americans who dares to go for universal jurisdiction implementation." During the 1991 Gulf War against Iraq, the U.S. attacked a bomb shelter in the Baghdad neighborhood of Al Amariyah. An F-117 stealth bomber hit the underground shelter with a laser-guided 2,000 bomb that ripped through the concrete. Moments later a second missile was launched directly into the opening, killing more than 400 people inside the shelter, including 261 women and 52 children. The U.S. claimed it was a "military communications center" and accused Saddam Hussein of deliberately placing civilians inside. A subsequent lawsuit, seeking to charge President George H.W. Bush and other U.S. officials, was filed in Belgium by family members of some of the victims. Under intense diplomatic pressure and threats, Brussels changed its universal jurisdiction law and threw out the war crimes case. Rahimi said the proper venue for prosecuting the Minab school massacre would be the International Criminal Court (ICC). Neither Iran nor the U.S. have formally recognized the court's jurisdiction. "Since we are not actually members of the ICC, we cannot file this complaint ourselves," he said, adding that Iran was encouraging other states and non-governmental organizations to submit requests to the court. "Perhaps we can say that the most important authority that can confront these aggressors--which is necessary--is the ICC." Brody said the rules of the ICC would technically allow Iran to accept its jurisdiction by lodging a declaration with the ICC's registrar, but it could not do so only in the interest of seeking an indictment against U.S. officials responsible for the Minab strikes. It would require that Iran accept the court's jurisdiction over Iranian officials as well, a move Tehran is unlikely to pursue, particularly given the U.S. hostility toward the ICC. Since his first term as president, Trump has waged war against the international court, sanctioning its personnel and openly defying the arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defense minister Yoav Gallant, who frequently visit the U.S. and, in Netanyahu's case, the White House. Trump is not the first U.S. president to attack the court. In 2002, President George W. Bush signed into law a bipartisan bill, subsequently known in the human rights community as the "Hague Invasion Act," permitting the use of military force to free any U.S. or allied personnel charged with war crimes by the court. | | ---|---|--- Mourners gather at a funeral for those who died in the U.S. strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh school in Minab. March 3, 2026. Photo by Morteza Akhondi. The cold reality of the post-World War II order is that international courts are intended to prosecute the "bad guys," the adversaries of the West, African dictators, and the political and military leaders in the former Yugoslavia. The Nuremberg Principles were never intended to apply to the U.S. and its friends. "We have to be a little bit realistic," said Askari. "We have the superpower against international law and of course the superpower and those who are in hegemonic power at the moment, they will do whatever they can to make sure that the legal instruments and the legal bodies, they cannot work against them." In late September, the Wall Street Journal that the Trump administration was preparing to intensify its campaign to abolish the ICC, including through sweeping sanctions. The administration, according to the Journal, wants to "cripple the court by prohibiting it from conducting transactions in U.S. dollars, cutting it off from much of the global financial system." While there are other venues, such as the International Court of Justice (ICJ), to pursue war crimes claims, there are numerous jurisdictional reasons why this path is not feasible. The U.S. withdrew its acceptance of ICJ jurisdiction in 1985, after Nicaragua successfully obtained a ruling that the U.S. violated international law by arming the Contra death squads and mining the Nicaraguan harbors. The U.S. announced a boycott of the court and denounced it as illegitimate. Israel joined the U.S. in withdrawing its own acceptance of ICJ jurisdiction. While Iran itself has accepted ICJ jurisdiction, it has done so only under the condition of reciprocity, meaning it cannot simply sue the U.S. there. In the case of the ICJ genocide case against Israel, South Africa relied on treaties to which Israel is a party to establish jurisdiction, namely the Genocide Convention. Brody said that to bring such a claim, Iran would need to identify a treaty that both it and the U.S. are parties to, which formed a clear legal basis for a proceeding. For decades, Iran was able to file claims against the U.S. at the ICJ by utilizing the 1957 Amity Treaty, which dates back to the rule of the Shah. Since the 1990s, Iran has filed several cases and won some rulings, including a 2016 case against the U.S. for illicitly seizing Iranian assets in violation of the bilateral Amity agreement and ordered the U.S. to pay compensation. In 2018, after the ICJ ordered the U.S. to ease some of its economic sanctions against Iran, the Trump administration denounced the court and withdrew from the Amity Treaty, a decision then-Secretary of State Mike Pompeo said was "frankly, 39 years overdue." Brody said he was not aware of an existing treaty between Iran and the U.S. that would clearly form the basis for a case against the U.S. at the ICJ related to the Minab strikes. While the most direct routes to pursuing international justice for the Minab victims appear limited for Iran, these challenges do not eliminate Iran's options. "The absence of a court with compulsory jurisdiction does not mean that the United States has no legal responsibility," Brody said. "It means that there may be no judicial forum in which Iran can compel the United States to answer for that responsibility." Brody said that Iran and other nations could pursue the establishment of a special tribunal on the crime of aggression against the U.S. "The most significant aspect of this conflict was not any individual strike, but the decision to wage war itself. President Trump authorized an armed attack against Iran in manifest violation of the UN charter--without approval from the United Nations Security Council, and in the absence of an imminent attack from Iran," he charged. "At Nuremberg [after World War II], aggression--the crime of waging an unlawful war of choice--was treated as 'the supreme international crime' because, as the Tribunal held, it contains within itself the evil of all the others. The crimes that flow from that unlawful war--including civilian casualties from airstrikes--are downstream consequences of the initial crime of aggression." But, Brody adds, "For the past 80 years, no one has been prosecuted for such acts of aggression because the major powers have made sure they weren't." In 2025, however, three dozen states--mostly European--established a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine. Operating in the Hague, the tribunal has a mandate to conduct trials in absentia against Russian officials. "There is no conceptual legal reason why states could not seek to create a comparable tribunal to investigate the political leaders who attacked Iran. The legal principle is identical: to launch a large-scale armed attack on another state without Security Council authorization, and in the absence of an actual or imminent armed attack, is a violation of the U.N. Charter," Brody said. "We can't disregard this principle simply because the perpetrators are Israel and the United States." Should Iran and other nations succeed in establishing such a tribunal and win a favorable ruling, enforcing the judgement is almost an unfathomable mission given the multi-decade U.S. track record of hostility toward international justice and law. "The Minab school strike is not an isolated tragedy. It is a symptom of a broader failure to comply with the law of armed conflict and to provide meaningful accountability when violations occur," said Brody. "Addressing that failure is not optional. It is a legal and moral imperative." | | ---|---|--- A bombed out classroom at the Shajareh Tayyebeh School. Photo by Hamid Vakili / Anadolu via Getty Images. Doutaghi, the international law scholar, said that while these legal pursuits are worthy, she does not have any faith that justice for the victims will emerge from these systems. "Documentation can establish a historical record; legal proceedings can establish responsibility; but neither changes the balance of power that enables aggression in the first place," she said. "For that reason, I believe Iran's most realistic path toward meaningful justice involves re-establishing deterrence and changing the balance of power. That means imposing political and material costs on aggression and making clear that attacks on Iranian civilians cannot be carried out without material consequences." "If the killing of Iranian children is followed only by documentation, condemnation, and memorialization, while the structures that permitted their killing remain untouched, then we have preserved the memory of the crime without addressing its material cause," Doutaghi added. "Justice must therefore mean both accountability for what happened and the transformation of the conditions that allowed it to happen." Salem, the Minab preschool teacher, said the families of the victims and the community will not find peace until there is retribution. "Everywhere you hear, 'We want revenge. Take revenge for our children,'" she explained. "When you don't take revenge, these crimes will be repeated." Minab Will Never Be the Same No single episode in recent Iranian history has impacted its broader society more deeply than the Minab school massacre. Every Iranian interviewed for this story broke down at some point during our interviews. After Dr. Movarekh, the director of the Minab hospital, finished sharing his memories from that day--which he had done for the first time since the attack--he turned to a colleague and confessed that he had hurt his hand because he was pushing his pen into his own skin in an effort to distract from the emotional pain he felt recounting that day. "If you read famous Iranian novels or poems, you cannot easily find a tragedy like what happened in real time, real life in the Minab incident," said Askari, the international law expert. "If you are a novelist, you are a poet, you imagine and you write--you try to make it as dark as possible to make sure that the reader is feeling profoundly sad," he added. "But I can tell you it is not comparable." Dr. Darvishi, the psychologist, is from an old Minab family. For her, the surviving children, parents, firefighters, teachers, and others directly impacted by the bombing are not just patients, but her community. "The city of Minab has experienced a tragedy and an incident that makes it impossible to return to the way things were before this," she said. "What happened in Minab is not something we can recover from with psychotherapy, humanitarian aid, and medication. The history of Minab has been transformed with this incident." | | ---|---|--- Yaghoub Yazdanpanah and Masoumeh Farahi Zadeh, parents of Fatemeh, who was killed by the U.S. missile strike on her school, at their home in Gurzang, Iran. Photo by Zohreh Saberi. Yaghoub, the father of Fatemeh, said he has depended on his Islamic faith to confront the killing of his daughter and his desire for justice. "The entire world should be terrified of this incident. What danger did the innocent children of Minab pose to the world that they had to attack a girls' school? They had to massacre six-year-old children? What kind of thinking is behind doing this to innocent children, children who don't know what war is, children who don't know what bleeding is, who don't know what enmity is?" he asked. "God willing, one day, somewhere, those responsible for this incident will be afflicted by this scandal. God was a witness to this and I am sure God's hand will enter this story and he will give them their just punishment." As Iranian students return to school this month, Darvishi and her colleagues are working to help families prepare in the aftermath of the horrors. "How can we ask these children to return to school? Because schools are no longer a safe place for those children. In our province, even throughout the entire country, families are worried about sending their children to school," she said. "In order for them to feel safe, we explain that we are in the process of negotiating and that we have very strong soldiers in the area of diplomacy and politics, and soldiers who are in the battlefield and they are defending us," Darvishi said. "We are explaining and telling them this will not happen again, although we are not sure." "As a mother, I don't have the heart. I don't have the heart to go school shopping because I am still mourning. I am mourning the children who are resting at the Flowerbed of Martyrs Cemetery," Salem said. "All of them are my children. They were my students. My colleagues--in one day, one moment, one hour, I lost 26 of my colleagues. Is there a crime worse than this?" Salem mentioned that students in the U.S. have been going back to school after their summer holidays. "Maybe people in America--many people around the world--have sympathized with the people of Minab, empathized with us. We are very grateful for them," she said. "Those who want to go shopping for their children for the start of the school year, maybe they will be reminded, maybe their hearts will ache again." Jawa Ahmad contributed to this report. clean_body: The Democrats are outspending us. Tonight decides whether we can answer back. | Fellow Patriot - I recorded a quick video for you on the campaign trail. I wanted you to see what this campaign really looks like: folks in red shirts, yard signs in the grass, South Carolinians who got up early on a weekend because they believe in this fight. But I'll be straight with you about what we're up against. Radical Democrats nationwide have already sent over $20 million to my opponent. That money is coming in from liberal donors across the country who see this seat as their chance to flip South Carolina blue. They're spending it on TV ads and mailers, and they have an army of paid staff to push the most radical agenda ever put before South Carolina voters. We can't match them dollar for dollar.We don't have to. That's why tonight's midnight deadline matters so much. It's our end-of-quarter deadline. When the reports go public, the media, the pundits, and the Democrats will all look at them to decide whether this race is competitive. A strong grassroots number tells them South Carolina isn't for sale. President Trump put it simply: "Run, Darline, Run!" I'm running as hard as I can. I need to know you're with me. name: Sherrod Brown
subject: I know it might seem daunting
body:
We can’t let this toss-up race swing in the GOP’s direction.
$2 million, Peter.
**That’s how much we need to raise before our final quarterly FEC deadline in less than 18 hours.** I know it might seem daunting, but if anyone can rise to the challenge, it’s this team.
**[Can I count on you to split $5 between my campaign and Wes Moore today?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260930-1.450GPG&refcode=em-20260930-1&t=1&akid=2022%2E1086043%2EIZR0jQ)**
We’ve made a massive dent in reaching our $2 million EOQ goal this month, thanks to the thousands of grassroots donors who have pitched in. But we have to close the gap.
I never ask lightly, because I know it’s not nothing to donate to a political campaign when you could spend that money elsewhere.
**But meeting our goal before the final FEC deadline of the midterms is crucial to keeping up our momentum and ensuring that this toss-up race doesn’t swing in the GOP’s direction.**
Unlike Republican Jon Husted, I’m not relying on one megadonor to write me a $2 million check -- I’m simply hoping you’ll split $5 or even just a few bucks between me and Wes Moore. Every little bit helps.
**[Will you make a donation right now to help us close the gap on our ambitious goal, flip Ohio, and take back the Senate?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260930-1.450GPG&refcode=em-20260930-1&t=2&akid=2022%2E1086043%2EIZR0jQ)**

I have few cards left to play.
With just a little over 12 hours left to reach our final end-of-quarter goal by tonight's deadline, we need to raise $650,000 more from emails like this to get back on track. If you're able to chip in $5, or even just a couple of bucks, it would be a huge help for our campaign.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/ca35aa63-fed6-4a13-8cda-86918c6a7376?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Now, I don't say any of this to alarm you.
Since this is a grassroots campaign, you deserve full transparency. It matters to me that my team and I keep you up to date on where we're at - good or bad.
That said, between President Trump and JD Vance smearing my name at in-state rallies, and recent polls showing my opponent Michael Whatley in striking distance of taking the slim lead, the timing of all this couldn't be worse.
National Republicans are trying to drown us out with more than $100 million worth of false attack ads - and here's the reality: That's what'll happen if they see we don't have enough funds to compete once our last quarterly finance report is released.
**To get over the hump, we either need lots of donations to come through the door today and tomorrow - or we need those who do chip in to give just a bit more.**
**[So I'm personally asking you to chip in $5 or anything to help me close the last $650,000 gap and keep up the fight to flip North Carolina and the Senate blue. I'm working as hard as I can to win this race, but I can't do it without you.](https://substack.com/redirect/ca35aa63-fed6-4a13-8cda-86918c6a7376?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Every dollar makes a difference. Thanks so much for all you do.
Roy Cooper

name: Citizens for Brad Smith
subject: We need your help to finish this race strong 💪

body:
This final month is critical. Here’s how you can help.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/c047fceeaf77/we-need-your-help-before-december-17461279?e=a4a0e00aa9)
---
| | | | |
---
|
---
| | Hi Peter,

Thank you for your continued involvement in this campaign, your trust in me, and the time, energy, and support you’ve given us throughout this race.
We’ve been working flat out since the Primary, and with just **34 days until Election Day** , we’re entering the final stretch.
**Before we get to the latest campaign updates, one important deadline: today is the final day of this campaign finance reporting period.**
If you are planning to contribute to the campaign, contributions received **before midnight tonight** will be included in this filing period.
[**CONTRIBUTE BEFORE MIDNIGHT TO BEAT GLENN**](https://us.list-manage.com/fN4DhJ76kfj?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8)
Every contribution helps fund the voter contact, mail, digital outreach, events, and organizing we’re carrying through Election Day.

### A Primary Win
First, thank you again for what you helped accomplish on August 11.It was a very close Primary, and our campaign reached voters across the district through an enormous volunteer effort. Together, we knocked more than 10,000 doors, while our mail and text programs reached more than 100,000 households.Volunteers talked with friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers. People spread the word. And voters showed up.
That victory belonged to everyone who helped build this campaign.

### The “Run Glenn Out of Town (Hall)” Tour
Since the Primary, we’ve launched a town hall tour with stops across all 11 counties of the district, giving residents an opportunity to hear directly from me, ask questions, and talk about the issues affecting their communities.
We also held an [online town hall](https://us.list-manage.com/N2Qfuk2qXqs?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8) for people who could not attend in person.Our campaign invited Glenn Grothman to participate in any or all of the events. So far, he has declined those invitations.

### **Endorsements**
I’m immensely proud to have earned these major endorsements:
* Senator Tammy Baldwin
* Congresswoman Gwen Moore
* WI AFL-CIO
* Sierra Club
* National Organization for Women (NOW)
* APWU
* AFT
* Smart Local 18
* IBEW Local 494
* ATU Local 998

You can read more about these exciting endorsements [here](https://us.list-manage.com/jBvSY41IsKT?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8).

### **Important Dates**
Please make note of these deadlines to help ensure your vote counts, and help loved ones do the same.
* **October 20** — early voting begins and goes through Friday, November 1.
* **October 30** — the deadline for requesting an absentee ballot. We strongly encourage you to hand in your ballot in person at your local municipal office instead of mailing it.
* **November 3** — in-person voting. You can register to vote at your designated polling location. Please check to ensure your location has not changed since the last election.
* [**Myvote.wi.org**](https://us.list-manage.com/8DO4Sr2Dftu?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8) is an excellent resource for all questions related to voting in Wisconsin.

**Now to November 3** We have just about 30 days til the general election, and we need your support now more than ever. Here is how you can help us finish strong!
---
| |
### 1️⃣ Donate and encourage others to join you
All donations go toward continuing to spread the word to undecided voters. Over 95% of our funds have been from Wisconsinites like you. You are helping fund text campaigns, mailers, yard signs, TV, radio and streaming advertisements, and digital billboards. We cannot ease off the gas, especially since many voters are only now starting to pay attention to who will be on their ballot.
---
| [DONATE NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/13tZBUtSxwx?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8)
---
| |
### 2️⃣ Sign up to reach voters
Knocking doors and making phone calls are the types of actions that win elections. There is still time — in fact, there’s no better time — for you to join us in reaching undecided voters. Each county office is organizing these efforts, and no experience is needed! If you need help locating your local office or organizer, please reply to this email and we’ll get you connected.
---
| |
### 3️⃣ Promote the campaign on social media
One of the simplest and most helpful things you can do is help spread the word online. Please like, follow, and share posts from @BradSmithforCongress on [Facebook](https://us.list-manage.com/14F1QDuK4xZ?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8), [Instagram](https://us.list-manage.com/oFTOqMECzGR?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8), [TikTok](https://us.list-manage.com/13YnZDh6LPN?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8), [YouTube](https://us.list-manage.com/hTu76l2eChw?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8), [BlueSky](https://us.list-manage.com/18goqm8AM4a?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8), and [X](https://us.list-manage.com/W5h2do9inq_?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8).
When more people help amplify our message, it expands our reach far beyond what paid ads can do.
---
| |
### 4️⃣ Attend upcoming events or invite family and friends
We’ve got the town halls and a number of other opportunities to chat with me. Showing up matters, and bringing others with you matters even more. Please join us at upcoming events and help spread the word across the 6th District: here is the [full list of events](https://us.list-manage.com/xSDt6kLAZ4b?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8).
Thank you again for being an important part of this team. With your help, we can move Wisconsin Forward, Together.
With gratitude,
Brad SmithCandidate for Congress, Wisconsin’s 6th District

_But I'll be straight with you about what we're up against._

Radical Democrats nationwide have already sent over $20 million to my opponent. That money is coming in from liberal donors across the country who see this seat as their chance to flip South Carolina blue. They're spending it on TV ads and mailers, and they have an army of paid staff to push the most radical agenda ever put before South Carolina voters.

**We can't match them dollar for dollar._We don't have to_. [We just have to close the gap enough to get our message out.](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=5e5fedc900034c9dad710140e6773fe0&_e=T5Qbt5Q4ERD65f-OgZnu_unECmyH519FzT22GWzoDXh5JSJwSXiUTf10xz54uU9qNRA0gyTy0U_7BVW81glfLs_gkhmJ8f6_CPd50LUUSy9jbKOGDZTWEofejYgZl6vc4ZHHU5Wf6Oy6349lpgiOqTbSVsweRzLsfuoViEW3bjPGuTIdA4LOOfJAJ9iL4gr6XONNrzPd8MLB-b7JtZzkLToN8YlxzqunohYbJt--FYuj88Jck3G4tQPH0vkvqgLBOJHp_KWBeyOVHPKCkKpgn71QAY4nHdr_nkN0Ti8xtagBwHDllEy_bnKql5LWc6ILFzyglYSz2wQ22wUJUfag9YY7hEODMGed_qOEFzwN-cfWwALJOua8-6oKDfSajG-mwN46smVlx0M80HtO2zvKIrXq0Y7PjsMotO5YnIYZSPYw-Ndz7_0F71PE6B3ON-7fZYkOu8Qatjz4UMRVvcTopkQWwLVqUK3phT-SFypg6T9AZCtCNcJgwhEvHh5FmNM2dnL6BlFgdopoNhHV77lOsgSsJaB5J6rJH0SjRaY4avbfFlnZt4WNndt7d6Anj4IgdQ8l0agHK2pO7JBwv2ucwDof98VjlCItK92TEr1zeWf73LbSjxKHBIkenbrMYvb0Lv1YcPVrUCRIVS5YKm_RwTFN_CUfeBRw0j1yU4hRZMflY1lS9evF61eQSnkntXLliRSqVSln5qhMaMzZ3MD4wVkbca64fo4WLA4o4CSBy7easovPbHp9Xy8JcufbisJscMA7TNZFt4z93UVhAy-p1A%3D%3D)**

name: Public Land Warriors
subject: The timber lobby bought the Forest Service
body:
A 45-million-acre corporate land grab
A 45-million-acre corporate land grab

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/Bt7AN4f4wV6oWOnhMoAt8Q~~/AAUS1hA~/fOEttAu3LyDuE5ilTscZl4dODf_l3oojsCMJmmzURzj6UnePWhfBogJ4VPtM06q-dhciNggyHsM_xKqhyB1G1TFFlL5d1w_6ppissHR7vWPKp9Er_EQ3KaOgHm6rA8H7)
| | | | Peter, How do you successfully execute a 45-million-acre corporate land grab? **Step one:** You take an executive who spent his career lobbying to chop down national forests. **Step two:** You appoint him as the Chief of the U.S. Forest Service. Step three: You wait for him to open the floodgates. **That is exactly what is happening right now in Washington.** Tom Schultz is the first-ever Forest Service Chief who didn't actually come from within the agency. Before this, he was the president of a timber trade association. Now, he is using his government authority to completely kill the 25-year-old "roadless rule," stripping protections from 45 million acres of untouched wilderness so his former employers can bulldoze roads and clear-cut the backcountry. The politicians rubber-stamping this heist are looking the American public in the eye and claiming they need to build logging roads into pristine habitats to "prevent wildfires." It is complete garbage. [**This is a 45-million-acre heist happening in broad daylight. Will you pitch in $10 today to our rapid-response war chest so we can expose this corruption?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/7Ij4PQNxX658sP_OX5iOQg~~/AAUS1hA~/3PLTuzKGdCE-4btkH19_olyzlta2nA1nSHzMSgfGemqxvdQuZ6uLn1NNVANNW92YXmkkVaaJtUdGIS5SMs5LePLxqDtRi2rCiPnHrtJ4XF_Vol7gBY1d22UL33x8UeebQmmva1XoUzJgSuIbv7fRKp2bRk_GrbTh2YAGlT0dPNEQb7NtXhgkWCy7Am0j1vg-DNC7pT8296cl5_j3NBwbq8tGxfvj4hwji_-9PgRptRYMk3podUktc_HRxWJR53uS) The Forest Service's _own data_ shows that wildfires are nearly three times as likely to start near roads because they bring in human ignition sources. They aren't trying to stop forest fires—they are using the threat of fires as a human shield for the timber lobby. And the lumber executives know it. They are literally bragging on corporate earnings calls, telling their Wall Street investors, "We know the new Forest Service chief." Schultz and the politicians enabling him think they can quietly liquidate the last remaining old-growth forests in America without facing any consequences. They expect you to be too exhausted by the news cycle to put up a fight. We are going to ensure that every hunter, angler, hiker, and voter knows exactly who allowed a timber lobbyist to sell off our national heritage. [**Will you chip in $10, $25, or $50 today to help us fund the backlash and hold them accountable at the ballot box?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/XoPYNkS24QVtIkjwJl9Fnw~~/AAUS1hA~/Axl7HN-JGSpNBRAn2gU0to1bR4pzzHE_hHkUQ6u9sHrr5LC4z4qnjjBEU-YXg13Rg6hwSMrwUcoFlvJZ81L9ifG1pKYXQ-HFmuGj9AeiGG2tV0RZkdViSsMxNVhLmOmbS0uSPzjFi7ypaJ6YzPnK8893f034Raf8kTkMzgSW4lhSTIIwfb9TwWh5mYZyKK9Hyy9goXssnOpZA7TXgmOYe1J-fZRLWYAmJ84YkE9qGu5mZbQQHVQWvNbffC6vb9b9) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/XoPYNkS24QVtIkjwJl9Fnw~~/AAUS1hA~/Axl7HN-JGSpNBRAn2gU0to1bR4pzzHE_hHkUQ6u9sHrr5LC4z4qnjjBEU-YXg13Rg6hwSMrwUcoFlvJZ81L9ifG1pKYXQ-HFmuGj9AeiGG2tV0RZkdViSsMxNVhLmOmbS0uSPzjFi7ypaJ6YzPnK8893f034Raf8kTkMzgSW4lhSTIIwfb9TwWh5mYZyKK9Hyy9goXssnOpZA7TXgmOYe1J-fZRLWYAmJ84YkE9qGu5mZbQQHVQWvNbffC6vb9b9) ** Thank you. | | Peter, The United States Senate has existed since 1789. In those 237 years, no Native American woman has ever served in it. The governor's office of any state? Same story. **Both of those doors could open on the same night on November 3rd.** **Peggy Flanagan** , a citizen of the White Earth Nation, is 1.8 points ahead in a race RealClearPolitics calls a toss-up — one hold away from that Senate first. **Deb Haaland** , a citizen of Laguna Pueblo, leads her governor's race in New Mexico — _a state that didn't let Native Americans vote until 1948_. From barred-from-the-ballot to the governor's desk, in one long lifetime. And **Mary Peltola** , a Yup'ik leader who already made history as the first Alaska Native in Congress, is in the dead heat Senate race that could decide the majority itself. subject: Why Chris’s election matters
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9227%2E582294%2EgfrHMd ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9227%2E582294%2EgfrHMd ]Chris Pappas for Senate

Hey, it’s
Vann, Chris’s husband. I wanted to reach out about his final
end-of-quarter deadline and what your support means to him.

I’ve watched how dedicated Chris is to this campaign: putting in the long
nights, late drives, and many conversations with Granite Staters. He loves
New Hampshire and knows what it means to give back to this state.

Now more than ever, we need leaders who will put the people first.

We can put a check on the chaos and corruption in Congress. That’s the
future Chris is fighting for. We just have to keep up the pace for the
last five weeks of this campaign.

This is a major $1 million goal, and Chris is counting on all of us to
step up. This is the last FEC deadline before Election Day, and I know
that Chris can depend upon this grassroots team.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260930_2.8DQ0ln&refcode=em20260930-2&t=1003&akid=9227%2E582294%2EgfrHMd ]There
are just hours to go. Will you chip in $5 or what makes
sense to you before tonight’s deadline? Let’s make it clear we have
Chris’s back.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260930_2.8DQ0ln&amount=5&refcode=em20260930-2&t=1022&akid=9227%2E582294%2EgfrHMd ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Vann

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/JHCA-09-Email-Sept2026-FR-EOQ?&refcode=E31830-20260930-EOQCoffee-Image-DeadlineEOQ&amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/JHCA-09-Email-Sept2026-FR-EOQ?&refcode=E31830-20260930-EOQCoffee-Image-DeadlineEOQ&amount=25]

Good morning, Peter!

I just woke up, had a cup of coffee, and wanted to send this to you first thing in the morning before I take my daughters to daycare.

Tonight is our last end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before the election. This is a big deal for our campaign because our report will be going public — and I’ll be honest, we are still falling short of our goal.

Donald Trump and his allies are spending millions on TV ads in California’s Central Valley and our fundraising has not been where we need it to be to respond effectively.

I’m really worried that if we do not reach our goal tonight, they’re going to have a major advantage against us and we won’t have the resources to fight back.

This is all leading up to tonight’s major FEC deadline. I have to make a big decision about how much budget we can put towards our get out the vote campaign. The truth is, we can't execute our strategy unless we hit our goal by midnight.

So I’m asking everyone on this team to step up. Will you please rush in a donation to help us keep California’s 9th district blue?

Here is a link: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/JHCA-09-Email-Sept2026-FR-EOQ?&refcode=E31830-20260930-EOQCoffee-SL-DeadlineEOQ&amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/JHCA-09-Email-Sept2026-FR-EOQ?&refcode=E31830-20260930-EOQCoffee-SL-DeadlineEOQ&amount=25]

Thank you for having my back,

— Josh

subject: 10 Things Worth Spending Money on Before It’s Too Late
body:
One decision could cost you $100,000--and the #1 item has a window that eventually closes.

| | |
---

**Good Morning!** What if **trying to save money now could end up costing you far more later?** One decision could potentially mean leaving**** more than $100,000 on the table. A test that costs around $150 could uncover a serious health issue before symptoms appear. And the #1 item on this week's list? **By the time you realize you need it, it may already be too late to get it.** In this week's****[_Flyover Focus_ ,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyszz9u8yAYgPHTmC3Wy_8wMHxLvqFKhy4ZLQgvNi2GyJBYuX2VqkfoAZ6f9FzO09mlnMr87la0PdYp1uu9TQX3lrF33CYKfUllbnvd-tJuWEIq81oLTgyYOoA5cPitKAk2IjLkBC3VBrTWVGiy2HiUGCgDd1UQveSAgkdDPSoVIjeKJPvSwHCgAqSQoxdOaqWid_woddSDAAyp1238rKn0BWN-1gdu47WuJNul91sb-L-BnQZ2etZ7v48eB3aC_x_mzV-O0n-RzYbbnnJOTb28eXUp__T9D9Yfln0HAAD__43ubtw) Ayla counts down **10 things actually worth spending money on as you get older** --ranked by how important they become with time. Some can make life better today. Others could protect your health, finances, or memories down the road. And a few come with windows that eventually close. We uncover the purchase many of us were taught to feel guilty about, the box sitting in your basement with an expiration date, and the financial decision researchers say only 4% of retirees get right. **➤ ****Some problems announce themselves.** The most expensive ones don't. body:
I figured it out as I went

| Peter, when I first stepped onto a college campus, I wasn't sure I belonged there.

I remember orientation before my first semester of undergrad. My parents came with me, as they always did, full of love and encouragement. But after the first session or two, my dad grew uncomfortable. He wore his old plaid shirt and cap, and the dirty shoes he wore to his construction job. He went back to the truck and waited for me to finish the rest of orientation.

**I understood why.** We were all new to this. I had no idea which extracurriculars to join, how to choose my classes, or what I was supposed to know about navigating college. My parents had always encouraged me to go — college was something they hadn't had the opportunity to do themselves — but they couldn't give me a roadmap for a journey they had never taken.

**I figured it out as I went, and somewhere along the way, I realized that not having a roadmap didn't mean there wasn't a path forward.** Sometimes, you have to take the next step and work hard because you believe something better is waiting on the other side.

Unfortunately, Mariannette Miller-Meeks is making it harder and harder to keep that optimism alive in our district. I hear from Iowans every day who want to get ahead but just can't see a way past the affordability crisis, our declining education system, or crushing medical bills.

I'm running to make sure families in our district have the chance to dream bigger, knowing their hard work is leading them toward a better future. Maybe the future they're working for changes over time; I know it did for me, but I want Iowans to know they can count on every opportunity to succeed.

**WHO AM I?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=03c073bb4b3b45c9a837e223774e3e62&_e=oi6QqKWsTCmHvrlhU8LNYFG5jjI7py55IyTkxhwwuUV72jGbTGQk9ryH4eWP2dlOWYBt84vQvH0s4-rMk61X9Pm3VwbvZ0un2-lvk7vmbQ3WPSxYMegFS_0kQuWm0F5mt3OrVB_J8Ftia-9tZux7EFeAaPTHbkUXQd3Qsq81PtRHJoAc_8L5LOLkdflYWJZy6NYUpS3EkVcofGn2beD1lzJSTZJfchbrSqqYXzauMaSc7q2VUIkf-bM2p5EEjfkjplc3-NA5pvHBcGZmmvuLtMMWihUFihMHc5oWQLrvmC6RMfFk7GyGF4HKdidUNSg3ShGjQ0rxDNXGQdLDURdxfAEi04aIbmxeFU7W8kx-8dc1G_JFrgJse971NkII8soAwr4Df1RKVibS5fMd8zU7NBNkEVzs-tLeRL2uy9wiAzRLp0mG8eo0nueGlst9YaLT6mDhQJETpyakYlCv2aWgbIwZGZ021Ibl7ADUKfUGXcytl-mSe6Flj1WU3qa0bNEE_VItINmtza-ZWoIIj0lYFg%3D%3D)

_Like I said, I’m Joe Males. I’m a Mexican-American who was adopted by two wonderful parents when I was four years old._

**At a young age, I joined the United States Marine Corps to defend our country and ultimately earned the rank of Sergeant before my discharge.** Once I entered civilian life, I started my entrepreneurial career owning a successful small computer business until my son took over the family business.

**Since the Democrats will want to use this to attack me, I will tell you: I was a former Democrat.** I switched over to the Republican Party during the Reagan era once I saw what the Democrats truly stood for. I’ve seen firsthand how today’s Democratic Party has abandoned working families. Every single day, I hear from constituents who are struggling with everyday challenges. I hear them, and I fully agree with them. It’s time for change in California.

**WHY DID I ENTER POLITICS?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=03c073bb4b3b45c9a837e223774e3e62&_e=oi6QqKWsTCmHvrlhU8LNYFG5jjI7py55IyTkxhwwuUV72jGbTGQk9ryH4eWP2dlOWYBt84vQvH0s4-rMk61X9Pm3VwbvZ0un2-lvk7vmbQ3WPSxYMegFS_0kQuWm0F5mt3OrVB_J8Ftia-9tZux7EFeAaPTHbkUXQd3Qsq81PtRFdbvqj1384jJHQKz2xXNjiZaKrhfQ2B5v2Oa2rgiiwuodMW3ZsY1uYHt4qDF-Llaef7rF3PdokDJBPdwJ-wl5TaAQwX4NTz3Pbf8rAj3j1dvwHXZluplCcuk_Eh6jVzaIsOgDX3FOr0iDtrxz3m1-yXAhSo0cNj8nSunPulXpEfHZ5R-Rhn1jPbB7JXGJC9J95rWYKxY7qhtn9SB3rOLc7P3q0MuaHvIziS03hTUmE2d0qzlWPL4l3oAn6tY8IMA_vZBMkfusG_SuLIK710Aq0Bss0S7FESle7G1-t0KlJDJoMyMjAIa3eg6cPP7szP0I74FpDNPkR2-pQTc2mJFpvoz07ikZuTDc5ZpMbdkLrg%3D%3D)

**In short, my son, Nicholas, was tragically stabbed to death and murdered in 2016.**

If you’re a parent, I’m sure you could imagine how devastating this was for me. Nicholas was only 28 at the time and did not deserve what happened.

He had followed in my footsteps and joined the Marine Corps. He was a father to two children – my grandchildren. When it happened, no one came forward with any information, and the case to find the killer went cold.

**I decided to take a stand, to fight for the rule of law and public safety so that no other family has to experience the same tragedy.** Five years later, I ran for City Council in Hemet. I won, and just a few months later, our amazing law enforcement found the killer and arrested him.

**WHAT ARE MY PRIORITIES AS YOUR NEXT CONGRESSMAN?** [](http://links.joemalesforca.com/u/click?_t=87a0bf2fd7e446429f4e355f2cd52f45&_m=03c073bb4b3b45c9a837e223774e3e62&_e=oi6QqKWsTCmHvrlhU8LNYFG5jjI7py55IyTkxhwwuUV72jGbTGQk9ryH4eWP2dlOWYBt84vQvH0s4-rMk61X9Pm3VwbvZ0un2-lvk7vmbQ3WPSxYMegFS_0kQuWm0F5mt3OrVB_J8Ftia-9tZux7EFeAaPTHbkUXQd3Qsq81PtQ2gcIClDq_y3X1NgztEq1z6wx6hDV8AApDbYsPNJ9P0iw6FUS6SRkEzb3oL5JASUWfm1AvsYZiGGjpLTXLu6rhh5htRyQiz51SX2F6GQEN_guk6cX_-P7G_rUVSNnr6-5FrGvJ52sEaeQ4UkQm6wfHk54OxnMG5yexYR4-tlM1IDAFQwzMziDUt5rxOGOU-tncignOFlCF3_SxzNAcl3E-wjJWf7HM439LxIrTc80bfXCcQlEUYttoGCh2vmfe4p6yKiLGQmKg2ZKp-ZK_IdTI6a-eB08vt_inwpo18s1MRFx-Dg5vFyFqQdcVY8EYKL8XAHpFH4BhZHrjMJ7-z7Qv7jlcIVgdDGfSIBbBcsARig%3D%3D)

_**As a former Democrat turned Republican, I know what the Democrat Party is supposed to represent. But ever since the Reagan era, they’ve continued to move farther and farther to the extreme left. Now, they stand for DEI, wokeness, putting Americans last, and doing everything they can to fight against President Trump.**_

**As a Hispanic American who lives in a border district and who was adopted by American parents, I fully believe in LEGAL immigration.** America is THE BEST COUNTRY IN THE WORLD! Millions of people around the world want to move here for the American Dream, for the opportunity of a better life, but they must do it THE RIGHT WAY.

**Our Southern Border has been porous under Joe Biden’s Administration.** Living in a border district, I’ve seen firsthand millions of illegal immigrants entering the country with the help of the dangerous Mexican Cartel, many through my hometown, bringing dangerous drugs like fentanyl, trafficking women and children, and committing heinous crimes on our side of the border. This needs to END, and I’m grateful for President Trump’s leadership on this. In Congress, I’ll always defend strong border security.

**On top of that, I am a firm believer in the America-First Movement.** After four years under Joe Biden’s leadership, America has become weak in every aspect. I already mentioned our border security, but our military, social life, and economy have all become weakened under the rule of DEI and wokeness.

**As a military veteran, it pained me to see the way Joe Biden withdrew from Afghanistan, giving the Taliban millions of dollars worth of high-level American military equipment, which they parade around.** Our weakened military presence allowed Russia to invade Ukraine and Hamas to launch terrorist attacks on Israel. clean_body: The Democrats are outspending us. Tonight decides whether we can answer back. | Fellow Patriot - I recorded a quick video for you on the campaign trail. I wanted you to see what this campaign really looks like: folks in red shirts, yard signs in the grass, South Carolinians who got up early on a weekend because they believe in this fight. But I'll be straight with you about what we're up against. Radical Democrats nationwide have already sent over $20 million to my opponent. That money is coming in from liberal donors across the country who see this seat as their chance to flip South Carolina blue. They're spending it on TV ads and mailers, and they have an army of paid staff to push the most radical agenda ever put before South Carolina voters. We can't match them dollar for dollar.We don't have to. That's why tonight's midnight deadline matters so much. It's our end-of-quarter deadline. When the reports go public, the media, the pundits, and the Democrats will all look at them to decide whether this race is competitive. Peter, we knew this was coming – even so, **it's not good.**
JD Vance has visited North Carolina to rally the GOP base and spread lies about me. MAGA loyalist Stephen Miller has gone on Fox News to rant and rave about me. President Trump’s DHS Secretary, Markwayne Mullin, has perpetuated lies against me on Newsmax, and the president himself has personally attacked me on social media in front of his millions of followers.
Now, Trump is upping the ante because this race in North Carolina could decide Senate control: MAGA Inc.’s super PAC is pouring millions into the effort to defeat me, bringing total Republican spending in this race to over $100 million (and counting).
**Peter, those attacks are working: A new poll shows our already narrow polling lead _is now within the margin of error._**
We warned folks that this was going to be a close race. In North Carolina, winning a U.S. Senate race by a "landslide" means winning, at best, 51% of the vote. That’s how competitive our state is, no matter what the pundits or the latest ratings say.
Unfortunately, many people seem to have turned their attention elsewhere, and as a result, we’re losing critical ground with just hours to go before our last quarterly FEC deadline of the campaign.
**I know we can get back on track, but not if we get complacent. Not without grassroots support from folks like you – right here, right now.[_That’s why I’m urgently asking, Peter: Will you chip in $5 or any amount to my campaign to help me meet our $5 million end-of-quarter goal, flip North Carolina and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1390&amount=5&t=8&akid=4001%2E124072%2EASw1p2)

body:
It's simple – doors, ballots, wins
This November is all or nothing for the Left. And they're counting on patriots like you to stay home.

| | | | Patriot,
---
Let me tell you why we're fired up about this November... Because 2026 is all or nothing for the Left. If they don't win the midterms, they know they'll be out of power for at least a decade. And right now, most polling in every swing state is a coin flip. Within the margin of error, either way. When it's that close, only one thing matters -- **_turnout._** Charlie Kirk built Turning Point Action to be the ballot-chasing machine that tips the scales in races like these. In 2024, we went 10 for 10. Every state we worked, President Trump won. **The formula is simple: Knock more doors. Chase more ballots. | | | | 34 DAYS TO ELECTION DAY NOVEMBER 3, 2026
---|---
HELP US REACH EVERY VOTER
We have just **34 days** to get our message into every corner of PA-11 and make sure voters know they have a choice on November 3.
| | Reaching voters takes resources. Billboards, digital and traditional media advertising, mail, signs, and organizing across the district all cost money. **Your contribution today** will help us reach more voters and build the campaign we need to win!
---|---
| [ DONATE TODAY ](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsEag4ErLzpEhPxLt9QUXR/8qkRHnWGGd1A)
---

**The Power of Personal Conversations**
With just weeks until the election, the most common question we hear is: “ _How can I help with the campaign?_ ”
In addition to the opportunities listed at the end of each newsletter, one of the most effective things you can do is talk with friends and family about the issues and candidates you support.**It may seem like a small act, but in a[June TED Talk](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsF30mRHkLv9rg1BGyPEFV/Aj5ObT6K1Ge2), Red Wine & Blue founder Katie Paris said conversations between friends can boost voter turnout by five to seven percentage points!**

---
Starting a political conversation can feel intimidating. These tips can help make it productive:
1. Think of someone who is frustrated by current events or someone who doubts voting in November will matter. Voting decisions often reflect personal values, and talking to someone who shares your values can provide more common ground than trying to connect across political party labels.
2. Bring up a current issue:
* “I’m worried about ________. What do you think?”
* “I know ________ matters to you. It matters to me too, which is why ________ concerns me.”
3. Listen with empathy. Focus on understanding the other person’s concerns, acknowledge what you hear, and seek common ground:
* “I get where you are coming from.”
* “I hear what you’re saying.”
* “I have the same concerns.”
4. Avoid using the word “but,” which can sound dismissive. Instead, try:
* “That’s why I can’t support policies that ________.”
* “That’s why I’m voting for ________.”
Use the conversation to share your values and explain what shapes your decision.
5. Know when to stop. Not every conversation will be productive.
6. One conversation may not be enough. Share relevant articles and invite the person to keep talking with you and – invite others to join the conversation.

---
The conversations with friends and family may seem small, but they can make a meaningful difference in November. Challenge yourself to have at least one each week. You can not only inspire others to vote on November 3rd but also help strengthen your community for the long term.

**Get Your Yard Sign!**
If you’ve been waiting to get a yard sign until closer to the election, the time is now! If you know any family, friends or neighbors who might want one, please send them our way! [Click here](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFVLUdi8i151w50enNxxZ/spxIYhZdXuHw) to reserve one now and a volunteer will deliver one to you or coordinate a pick-up.
---
---
## **Week in Review**
---

**Fundraiser with Representative Mary Gay Scanlon****** At a recent fundraiser held in Lancaster, Nancy was joined by U.S. Representative Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-5), one of the first women to join Pennsylvania’s congressional delegation in 2019. We were honored by her attendance and her vision for a Democratic-led House in 2027!
---
---

**Celebrate the Slate!** On Friday, September 25, Nancy joined fellow York County candidates at Collusion Tap Works. Attendees were invited to donate new children’s books to York County libraries in support of [Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFxgCq8X470CC8q2cMhfd/H2pyd2Ok5Web). Nancy spoke with voters concerned about rising food, housing, and fuel costs—underscoring that affordability is on everyone’s mind.
---
---

**Hempfield Area Dems Host a “Meet the Candidate” Forum****** On Sunday, Nancy joined State Sen. James Malone and PA House District 41 candidate Brad Chambers at a Lancaster County Meet the Candidates forum hosted by the Hempfield Area Democratic Committee (HDAC). They addressed audience concerns about immigration, data centers, and other issues. Thank you to everyone who attended despite the inclement weather and to HDAC for organizing this informative event.
---
---

What he wants is a guarantee of millions in federal funding. He says he will route it as dark money so nobody can trace it. He also says Collins should know who it came from.The super PAC chief agreed. So the fake charity was not there to hide the money from Susan Collins. It was there to hide it from the people of Maine. The contractor got his federal work. He later told the FBI his products were of no real value to the Navy and would never be deployed. He got the contract. You got the bill. Nobody should be surprised.**Ninety-seven billionaires and their spouses have poured $9.8 million into her operation since the start of last year and not one of them lives in Maine.** Twenty-nine years in the Senate and that is who shows up to fund her. He later told the FBI his products were of no real value to the Navy and would never be deployed. He got the contract. You got the bill. Nobody should be surprised.Ninety-seven billionaires and their spouses have poured $9.8 million into her operation since the start of last year and not one of them lives in Maine. Twenty-nine years in the Senate and that is who shows up to fund her. Troy Jackson is a fifth generation logger from Allagash, a town of a few hundred people at the top of Maine. No corporate PAC money. No billionaires. No shell companies. Chip in what you can: | | | | | | | | | | A poll this week has this race inside the margin of error. Her super PAC has $24 million in ads already booked. Jackson got in this summer with nothing and raised 5.3 million dollars on ActBlue in half a month, almost all of it small. One of these campaigns is funded by people who want something from Washington. The other is funded by people who live in Maine. Thirty four days. Thank you for joining the fight. Peter, I wanted to send you one last note before tonight's midnight fundraising deadline.

It's not lost on me that, in just a few weeks, voters across St. Louis will decide who they want fighting for them in Congress.

Look, I grew up here. St. Louis made me who I am. And every single day I get to represent this community in Congress is an honor I'll never take for granted. We've accomplished a lot together, _but I know there is so much more work ahead of us._

I want to keep fighting to lower costs for working families.

To protect access to healthcare.

To bring federal resources and good-paying jobs home to St. Louis.

And to make sure the people I represent always have someone in Washington willing to stand up for them.

But first, **we have to make it through November.**

Tonight at midnight will mark the start of our final end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before Election Day, and I'm hoping you'll help make sure we enter these last few weeks with everything we need to bring this thing home.

Football season is officially here in Texas, and last Friday, I had the pleasure of hanging out with Adrianne Palicki, aka Tyra Collette from _Friday Night Lights_. _(Yes, that Friday Night Lights!)_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3fda3998-ec86-42cb-8c53-de778c0fa043?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It really doesn't get much more Texan than bright lights and a great football game. And Cedar Hill and Lancaster High Schools certainly put up a fight.
Watching those two teams battle it out on the field got me thinking about how football can be a lot like running a campaign.
You need a solid game plan, a team that knows what's at stake, and people willing to put in the work play after play.
That sounds a lot like what we've been doing on the ground here in Texas.
We've driven thousands of miles, traveling across the state and showing up in communities that have historically been Republican strongholds. It was important to me that _all_ Texans knew that I would show up and fight for them.
As families continue to face skyrocketing electricity costs and property tax increases year after year, they deserve a Governor they can trust to play defense for working families -- not run up the score for wealthy special interests.
Texans deserve a seat at the table, and it's past time we put Greg Abbott back on the sidelines and start moving Texas toward a better future.
But we're up against Greg Abbott and his multimillion-dollar war chest. At the start of 2026, he had more than $100 million cash on hand, and right now, we're being outspent 10-to-1.
**That means for every $1 we spend, Greg Abbott can spend $10.**
That could be the difference between Greg Abbott launching an attack ad against me and our campaign having the resources to fight back with the truth -- or letting his attacks go unanswered. Because he's going to be using the political fundraising machine he's spent decades building right up until the clock runs out.
**But I know we can fight back because I have all of you on my team.**
And you don't win a football game alone. You win it with everyone on your team doing their part.
Greg Abbott and his wealthy special-interest backers may have a massive financial advantage, but I believe in the movement we've built to put Texans first.
**We 're in the fourth quarter now, and time is running out.**
**[I've got just one play left to call, and I'm hoping you're willing to get in the game. If you can, will you please chip in $5 or whatever you can today to help us keep our ads on the air, reach voters across Texas, and keep this grassroots campaign moving in these final few weeks before Election Day?](https://substack.com/redirect/3fda3998-ec86-42cb-8c53-de778c0fa043?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE NOW ->](https://substack.com/redirect/3fda3998-ec86-42cb-8c53-de778c0fa043?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Because when that final whistle blows, I want the people of Texas to know we left everything we had on the field.
Clear eyes, full hearts, can't lose.
-- Gina

clean_body: And I'm counting on each of you to help us land a win on Election Day | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more And I'm counting on each of you to help us land a win on Election Day Sep 30 | | | | | | | | | | | Football season is officially here in Texas, and last Friday, I had the pleasure of hanging out with Adrianne Palicki, aka Tyra Collette from Friday Night Lights. (Yes, that Friday Night Lights!) | | ---|---|--- It really doesn't get much more Texan than bright lights and a great football game. And Cedar Hill and Lancaster High Schools certainly put up a fight. Watching those two teams battle it out on the field got me thinking about how football can be a lot like running a campaign. You need a solid game plan, a team that knows what's at stake, and people willing to put in the work play after play. That sounds a lot like what we've been doing on the ground here in Texas. We've driven thousands of miles, traveling across the state and showing up in communities that have historically been Republican strongholds. It was important to me that all Texans knew that I would show up and fight for them. As families continue to face skyrocketing electricity costs and property tax increases year after year, they deserve a Governor they can trust to play defense for working families -- not run up the score for wealthy special interests. Texans deserve a seat at the table, and it's past time we put Greg Abbott back on the sidelines and start moving Texas toward a better future. But we're up against Greg Abbott and his multimillion-dollar war chest. At the start of 2026, he had more than $100 million cash on hand, and right now, we're being outspent 10-to-1. That means for every $1 we spend, Greg Abbott can spend $10. That could be the difference between Greg Abbott launching an attack ad against me and our campaign having the resources to fight back with the truth -- or letting his attacks go unanswered. Because he's going to be using the political fundraising machine he's spent decades building right up until the clock runs out. But I know we can fight back because I have all of you on my team. And you don't win a football game alone. You win it with everyone on your team doing their part. Greg Abbott and his wealthy special-interest backers may have a massive financial advantage, but I believe in the movement we've built to put Texans first. We 're in the fourth quarter now, and time is running out. Because when that final whistle blows, I want the people of Texas to know we left everything we had on the field. Clear eyes, full hearts, can't lose. -- Gina * | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Gina Hinojosa PO Box 300095, Austin, TX 78703 ? ?

name: Office of the First Lady
subject: News from First Lady Moore: A New Era for Maryland's Horse Industry
body:
| | | | Hello Friends and Fellow Marylanders, It’s hard to believe we’re already entering the final three months of the year. Looking back, I'm proud of the work we've accomplished to truly build a state that leaves no one behind. In the past few months, I’ve seen our work produce meaningful results. I’ve been honored to champion efforts to advance literacy within our communities, curb chronic absenteeism among our students as we start a new school year, and build economic growth by securing the future of our horse industry through a new era for Maryland’s iconic Preakness Stakes. Our administration is not slowing down and remains committed to uplifting our core priorities centered on Maryland communities, workers, and children. As we settle into fall, let’s continue to work together to build a state that our future generations would be proud of. Take Care, **First Lady Dawn Moore** |
* * *
---
## **KEEPING UP WITH**
# **THE FIRST LADY**
### **Maryland's Horse Industry Enters New Era Under Moore-Miller Administration**
Under the leadership of Governor and First Lady Moore, Maryland's horse industry is chartering a new path focused on sustaining its future.
Since taking office, the administration has demonstrated its commitment to the industry through investing record funding in the historic Pimlico Race Track and Park Heights neighborhood, creating the Preakness Festival to bring economic growth and expand community outreach, establishing the Maryland Horse Industry Strategic Plan, owning the intellectual property rights of the Preakness Stakes, and securing a new deal for the Preakness Stakes programming.
Marylanders can expect major changes in 2027, as the Preakness Stakes comes home to Baltimore on a new race day,**Sunday May 23, 2027**.
Check out all of the latest news below.
| | **[The Preakness Stakes Moves to Sunday with New Race Day Schedule](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress-releases%2Fgovernor-moore-announces-new-preakness-race-schedule/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/oHLW5nml74YYj3WYgrpiG_un32PpUWo_lM3OcjZVTEM=452)** Beginning in 2027, the Preakness Stakes will move one week later on the calendar, to be contested three weeks after the Kentucky Derby.
The 2027 Preakness Stakes moves to _**Sunday, May 23**_ and the Black-Eyed Susan Stakes will be showcased on _**Saturday, May 22,**_ both airing on NBC and Peacock. These changes are part of the Maryland Jockey Club and NBC Sports multi-year partnership extension to present the Preakness Stakes through 2032.
---|---|---
| | **[Maryland Fully Owns Preakness Intellectual Property Rights After Final Acquisition](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress-releases%2Fgovernor-moore-announces-maryland-fully-owns-preakness-intellectual-property-rights/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/5-5pELrxBkmHlKcstw8To9m-snt1g9ZOIPbKr1ZZYLY=452)** The State of Maryland has completed its acquisition of the Intellectual Property (IP) Rights to the Preakness Stakes and Black Eyed Susan from 1/ST Racing, ensuring that the race will call Baltimore and Maryland home well into the future, and that the State remains in firm control of Maryland’s multi-billion dollar equine industry.
---|---|---
| | **First Lady Sets Vision for 2027 Preakness Festival** The First Lady is proud to bring the Preakness Festival back to Baltimore in 2027. Marylanders can expect new events and family gatherings across the state, among some of the festival’s most anticipated events — the Governor’s Classic Golf Tournament, Preakness Festival concert, and a collaboration with the George “Spider” Anderson Music & Arts Festival.
---|---|---
| | **[Celebrate Maryland's Equine Industry this October during "Horse Month"](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fmarylandhorse.com%2F/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/jjxwbcxu-o7LHJ8zYvWxCQr4S-cEiSt5AcWqz_u4ZAs=452)** The First Lady is calling on all Marylanders to celebrate Horse Month by experiencing the dozens of events showcasing more than 5,000 horses, ponies, and donkeys across the state. Learn more about Maryland’s horse industry and events at [Visit Maryland](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.visitmaryland.org%2Fthings-do%2Fmaryland-horse-collection/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/9Bo0Ahz-LlM6z3tMPm5hL7qlOLaLdRbQTz14UrCVmyw=452). Maryland is also home to internationally renowned events in October including [Jim McKay Maryland Million Day](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fmarylandmillion.com%2F/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/YtkExsmOgoc4ZiNc3hr0RB5yAqWoBwG5oQEjolt8RZ0=452) at Laurel Park and the [Washington International Horse Show](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwihs.org%2F/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/rU-tokn_bDl1MsL-UITLipBdDQSP3TQZ97ZzLkhyN_o=452) in Prince George’s County. Together, these events are expected to attract more than 100,000 spectator visits and millions of online views, putting Maryland’s vibrant horse industry on display for audiences near and far.
---|---|---
* * *
---
### [First Lady Moore Brings #ReadMoreMaryland to the Baltimore Book Festival](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.flickr.com%2Fphotos%2Fmdgovpics%2Falbums%2F72177720335726452%2F/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/QCry2LMw8Rs7uE6mNYb8criXEpXkkIXo5yAQs3MwihQ=452)
First Lady Moore joined the 27th annual Baltimore Book Festival to read to young Marylanders through the [Charm City Cultural Cultivation](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.charmccc.org%2F/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/j0WOa0omrT8f4FE47f6JxFYG1b50juGUuFHoTOE8HV8=452)’s “Reading is Freedom” initiative, created by artist Derrick Adams and [Emerson Collective](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.emersoncollective.com%2F/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/Da0XUYwiMqKK_5hJW8rehgsWFH0-t1hBntnruEpczJI=452).
As a special guest reader at the Stoop Reads activation, she brought to life “Rain and the Reading Horse” to more than 50 people. Each child read along with their free copy of the book. The Maryland Jockey Club also donated free horse themed coloring books to showcase the state's rich equine industry.
The Stoop Reads had multiple special guest readers including Councilwomen Odette Ramos, Reading Rainbow's Mychal Threets, and Wanda Durant.
This event highlights the First Lady’s [#ReadMoreMaryland](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fleadership%2Ffirst-lady%2Fpress-releases%2Fgovernor-and-first-lady-moore-host-young-marylanders-readmoremaryland-campaign/1/010001a0f2d7361e-97129367-b92d-46b9-b859-472a02bf0949-000000/2-qmiS5_5aA1-v0cWq34pN055dJaIXkQyu8KISo_WBU=452) campaign, which encourages Maryland youth and their parents to read. Maryland has made massive gains in literacy achievement, and the administration continues to work within each community to advance literacy and empower its young people to reach their full potential.

clean_body: | | | | Hello Friends and Fellow Marylanders, It’s hard to believe we’re already entering the final three months of the year. Looking back, I'm proud of the work we've accomplished to truly build a state that leaves no one behind. In the past few months, I’ve seen our work produce meaningful results. I’ve been honored to champion efforts to advance literacy within our communities, curb chronic absenteeism among our students as we start a new school year, and build economic growth by securing the future of our horse industry through a new era for Maryland’s iconic Preakness Stakes. Our administration is not slowing down and remains committed to uplifting our core priorities centered on Maryland communities, workers, and children. As we settle into fall, let’s continue to work together to build a state that our future generations would be proud of. Take Care, First Lady Dawn Moore | KEEPING UP WITH THE FIRST LADY Maryland's Horse Industry Enters New Era Under Moore-Miller Administration Under the leadership of Governor and First Lady Moore, Maryland's horse industry is chartering a new path focused on sustaining its future. Since taking office, the administration has demonstrated its commitment to the industry through investing record funding in the historic Pimlico Race Track and Park Heights neighborhood, creating the Preakness Festival to bring economic growth and expand community outreach, establishing the Maryland Horse Industry Strategic Plan, owning the intellectual property rights of the Preakness Stakes, and securing a new deal for the Preakness Stakes programming. Marylanders can expect major changes in 2027, as the Preakness Stakes comes home to Baltimore on a new race day,Sunday May 23, 2027. Hi friend, it’s Pete Buttigieg.
Politics works best when it's built from the ground up. The most impactful work in any election happens when people in a community decide to organize, connect with good candidates, and engage directly with their neighbors.
I've seen that the candidates who win close races never do it alone. Often they win with the backing of a strong state party, one that recruits candidates for seats others have overlooked, trains the volunteers who knock the doors, and keeps organizing through the off years so that every campaign starts on firmer ground than the last.
That work rarely gets much attention, but it's often what decides a close race. And right now, those efforts can make a huge impact in Nevada.
This November, Nevadans will choose their next governor, decide competitive races for Congress, and elect the state legislators who will shape their state for years to come.
Close states like Nevada are won by organizing: conversations at the door, volunteers who stay with it through Election Day, neighbors bringing one more person at a time into the work. That kind of effort takes time to build and resources to sustain, and what we do in the next few weeks will determine how strong it is by November.

clean_body: | | | | Hi friend, it’s Pete Buttigieg. Politics works best when it's built from the ground up. The most impactful work in any election happens when people in a community decide to organize, connect with good candidates, and engage directly with their neighbors.
