Often they win with the backing of a strong state party, one that recruits candidates for seats others have overlooked, trains the volunteers who knock the doors, and keeps organizing through the off years so that every campaign starts on firmer ground than the last. That work rarely gets much attention, but it's often what decides a close race. And right now, those efforts can make a huge impact in Nevada. This November, Nevadans will choose their next governor, decide competitive races for Congress, and elect the state legislators who will shape their state for years to come. Close states like Nevada are won by organizing: conversations at the door, volunteers who stay with it through Election Day, neighbors bringing one more person at a time into the work. **Wednesday, September 30, 2026 -**_****_
**Iran** : Iran says it received U.S. response to Strait of Hormuz proposal. U.S. sanctions ten entities in China, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia over Iran arms procurement. **Palestine** : Israeli strike on vehicle kills six in Gaza City as death toll since Tuesday reaches 13. Israeli forces raid homes, settlers attack Palestinian property across the occupied West Bank. Gaza child mortality more than doubled in 2025 amid Israeli attacks. Qatar PM: Hamas agreed to release all civilian hostages on October 7.
**Lebanon** : Lebanese soldier, civilians wounded in Nabatieh as Israeli ceasefire violations continue across the south. Four in five Lebanese households struggle to afford basic needs as conflict deepens crisis.
**U.S.** :**** Senate blocks resolution on occupied West Bank. Supreme Court allows President Donald Trump's third-country deportation policy to resume. ICE plans to hire 5,000 more officers by year's end. California passes law banning shock gloves for law enforcement. Tech executives sign "morally binding" AI accord at White House lunch with Trump. DHS confirms $20 million in taxpayer funds spent on pro-Trump ads, drawing bipartisan criticism. IRS to add citizenship question to tax forms. Trump administration preparing to auto-enroll all children in Trump Accounts before midterms. Trump's ban on $1 billion in Canadian imports takes effect. Federal prosecutors charge Wilber Garces Perez with assaulting ICE officer in Austin shooting. Senate GOP leaves Trump's $350 billion defense funding request in limbo before recess.
**International** :**** Commercial plane traveling from UAE to Israel forced to land in Saudi Arabia after fight between pilots. Scandal rocks Flavio Bolsonaro campaign ahead of first-round election in Brazil. Amnesty: Mali army, Wagner mercenaries killed at least 34 civilians in seven incidents. UN renews Haiti security force mandate. Belgium to transfer three F-16s to Ukraine by year's end, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says. Russian Tu-95 bomber crashes during training, killing six crew. Lithuania offers to pay for permanent US troop presence, PM says. UN says North Korea violated armistice; North Korea dismisses DMZ mine blast findings as "farce." Afghanistan says it killed 41, captured 62 insurgents crossing from Pakistan in three days. Somali pirates kill five crew members before tanker rescue by Puntland forces. Fighting between SPLM-N, Otoro tribe kills over 500 in Sudan's Nuba Mountains. Malaysia begins sending nearly 1,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar despite safety concerns. 300,000 join French civil servant strikes; student protests turn violent nationwide. UK's Burnham vows sweeping public service expansion in first conference speech as PM.

* * *
# Iran
* **Iran says it received U.S. response to Hormuz proposal:** Iran [received](https://substack.com/redirect/60d4af88-baee-4bf6-9ecf-62d0045aeaad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a U.S. proposal amid indirect talks over reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a government spokesperson said, without disclosing details.
* Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented the proposal to President Masoud Pezeshkian during a cabinet meeting after briefing officials on his meetings in New York, Mohajerani said.
* **U.S. sanctions ten entities in China, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia over Iran arms procurement** : The Treasury Department sanctioned ten individuals and companies, including representatives and technology firms based in China, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia (and three based in Iran), accusing them of procuring weapons and parts for Iran's Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics.
* The sanctions targeted Hong Kong-based EC Mojo Technology Co Ltd, which the U.S. has accused of supplying electronic components and evading export controls.
* The U.S. also sanctioned the Saudi-based Cavalier Dynamics for Technologies Company.
* **U.S. offers 40 million barrels from strategic reserve:** The Trump administration [offered](https://substack.com/redirect/e5131f78-1eb1-48d3-af95-61b3b60124ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to lend up to 40 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve on Tuesday, as fuel prices remain near record highs seven months into the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.
* The barrels are the last tranche of the 172 million the U.S. pledged in March to an International Energy Agency release of 400 million barrels coordinated among about 30 countries.
* The release is structured as an exchange, not a sale: companies borrow the oil and later return it with additional barrels as a premium. Bids are due on October 6.
* The reserve held 283.8 million barrels as of September 25, its lowest level in 44 years, according to Energy Department data.

* **Qatar PM says Iran war pushed country into budget deficit:** Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani [called](https://substack.com/redirect/8cc8c210-a43c-4489-85bb-b950ac54f083?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the war on Iran one of the biggest crises in Qatar's history, telling Piers Morgan that LNG exports through Hormuz are "barely happening."
* He was asked about a reported $24 billion in lost gas sales, an IMF forecast of more than 8% contraction this year, an 80% drop in visitors and hotels 60% empty, and said "many of those numbers" were accurate.
* He said after an Iranian missile hit Qatar's LNG facility the country now faces a budget deficit. It has cut secondary projects but not salaries, leaning on its sovereign wealth fund.
* "It's not a structural contraction for our economy," he clarified, saying LNG output will return once damaged trains are repaired.
* **Three tankers struck by unknown projectiles in Strait of Hormuz:** Three tankers were struck by projectiles of unknown origin while transiting the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours, according to incident reports from the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). One of the crude oil tankers was hit while transiting inbound.
* **No explosives found in vans near RAF Fairford, UK police say:** No explosive devices were found in three vans linked to five men arrested near RAF Fairford, the British airbase used by U.S. forces for strikes on Iran, UK counterterrorism police said. Police said a quantity of petrol was recovered and the investigation remains ongoing.
* The five British nationals were arrested Sunday on suspicion of terrorism before being released on bail Monday.
* U.S. President Donald Trump criticized the suspects' release and suggested they "might be" connected to Iran. Iran has denied involvement, and UK authorities have not publicly established a foreign link.
* **Iran executes two more over January protests:** Iran executed two men on Wednesday on charges related to violence during nationwide anti-government protests in January, according to state news.
* The men took part in protests in the northeastern city of Mashhad that left four security officers dead and confessed to setting fires, the judiciary determined, damaging public property, and stabbing a member of Iran's paramilitary force.
* Iran has executed dozens of people on charges related to the January protests in what Amnesty International has [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e190556a-24dd-4f58-90c7-eadf222c50ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) followed "torture-tainted grossly unfair trials by Revolutionary Courts."

# Yemen
* **UAE vice president visits Saudi Arabia for first time since rift** : UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan [visited](https://substack.com/redirect/79c637cf-b552-44a9-a67b-34970ae2d942?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Saudi Arabia Tuesday and met with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, the first senior UAE official to visit the kingdom since a rift emerged last December.
* It remains unclear whether Saudi Arabia's push for international support against Ansarallah extends to reengaging the UAE, once its main partner in the Yemen war.
* The two countries' tensions emerged after UAE-backed southern Yemeni separatists advanced near Saudi borders, prompting a Saudi airstrike on a UAE-linked weapons shipment at Mukalla port. The UAE subsequently announced a full withdrawal of its forces from Yemen.
* **Ansarallah ballistic missiles strike Saudi-backed forces ' camps in southern Yemen:** Nearly 20 soldiers and officers are believed to be among the dead and wounded, according to OSINT reports, after an Ansarallah ballistic missile [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/80376f85-35d6-442e-9ffe-dfdfe9ceb211?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Saudi-backed Homeland Shield Forces military camp in the Al-Qawah area on the southern Yemeni coast on Tuesday.
* Three ballistic missiles also struck the camp of the Fourth Mountain Infantry Brigade, south of Al-Turbah.
* Saudi-backed forces claimed to have carried out 414 strikes targeting Ansarallah positions over the past 24 hours, according to the armed forces spokesperson.

# Palestine
* **Israeli strike on vehicle kills six in Gaza City as death toll since Tuesday reaches 13:**
* Six Palestinians were killed and 15 others wounded on Wednesday when an Israeli [strike](https://substack.com/redirect/eff9eb38-4fd1-4f7a-9047-513bf84705cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) hit a vehicle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City, according to WAFA.
* A woman was killed in an Israeli strike on an apartment near Al-Shifa Medical Complex.
* Four Palestinians, including two children, were wounded when an Israeli drone struck a tent sheltering displaced people west of Khan Younis, while two others were critically wounded by Israeli gunfire southeast of Deir al-Balah.
* At least 13 Palestinians have been killed and 42 wounded in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip since Tuesday.
* **Israeli forces raid homes, settlers attack Palestinian property across the occupied West Bank:**
* **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/080fb3fd-9293-48b8-a0aa-f8413ba0b0b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) widespread raids across the governorate, storming homes in Kafr Zibad, Kafr Jammal, Kafr Abbush, Kafr Sur, Far'un, Attil, Deir Al-Ghusun, Shuweika, and several neighborhoods of Tulkarm city on Wednesday, WAFA reported. Forces converted some homes into military posts, set up checkpoints and detained several Palestinians, including former prisoners.
* **Jenin:** Israeli forces [ordered](https://substack.com/redirect/d4158ae3-b9c9-4ee3-86b3-94b145e7fd98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) families out of homes in Jenin's Old City and Marah Saad and converted several buildings into military posts. Forces were deployed across the city and along the Jenin-Nablus road and closed iron gates at entrances to nearby towns and villages.
* **Ramallah and Al-Bireh:** In Taybeh, settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/42b6b18e-8575-46bd-9ac7-392f36e96286?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a family home, beating family members and spraying them with pepper spray, injuring a teenage boy.
* **Bethlehem:** Settlers [destroyed](https://substack.com/redirect/35c54c45-d0c9-43fc-97c2-35f0c240c19d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a drinking-water pipeline supplying a Bedouin community of around 800 Palestinians in Al-Rashaydeh, southeast of Bethlehem.
* **Nablus:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/969832ff-4508-4afe-9182-8954b1a46542?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several neighborhoods of Nablus and the town of Deir Sharaf, firing stun grenades and tear gas. An 80-year-old man was hospitalized after soldiers beat him, while Palestinians were detained, including three 14-year-old boys in Deir Sharaf.
* **Gaza child mortality more than doubled in 2025 amid Israeli attacks:** The mortality rate for children under five in Gaza more than doubled to 33.4 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2025, up from 13.6 in 2022, according to the Health Ministry's first official mortality report since 2022.
* The ministry estimates the rate would be 15.8 without deaths caused by the war.
* Israel's direct attacks were the leading cause of death in Gaza in 2025, accounting for 70.1% of the 24,650 recorded deaths.
* **Qatar PM: Hamas agreed to release all civilian hostages on October 7:** Hamas [agreed](https://substack.com/redirect/e85cddd0-9db2-41ff-84d9-185e5b3393d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the first day of the war on Gaza to "release all civilian hostages," asking only for a ceasefire window to get them out, and Israel refused to even "entertain the idea," Qatar's Prime Minister confirmed.
* "We got an agreement" to release "all the civilian hostages," Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani told Piers Morgan. Israeli officials replied that if Hamas wanted to free them, it should do so without a pause in fighting, he said.
* His on-record account follows a Haaretz report this month that he relayed the offer to then-Mossad chief David Barnea on the evening of October 7.

# Lebanon
* **Lebanese soldier, civilians wounded in Nabatieh as Israeli ceasefire violations continue across south:** A Lebanese soldier and at least three civilians were wounded in an explosion in Nabatieh Al-Fawqa on Wednesday.
* Elsewhere in southern Lebanon, an Israeli Merkava tank [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/85990e8a-a163-49a9-962c-afda552e458a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two shells toward a home in Bra'shit early Wednesday, the state's National News Agency reported. Israeli artillery also struck Haddatha, Kfar Tebnit, Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, Bra'shit, and Wadi Al-Salouqi overnight, while Israeli forces carried out two explosions near Beit Yahoun and Aita Al-Jabal.
* **Four in five Lebanese households struggle to afford basic needs as conflict deepens crisis:** Four in five households in Lebanon are struggling to afford basic necessities, with 22% reporting their children had gone to bed hungry in the previous two weeks and 14% reporting at least one child working, according to a new UNICEF [report](https://substack.com/redirect/975f79cc-e14e-4204-8be1-3239644af17b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Since March 2, at least 261 children have been killed and 1,056 injured in Israeli attacks, averaging seven children killed or wounded each day over six months, UNICEF said.
* Some 436 schools have been damaged or destroyed, putting around 100,000 children at risk of being without a classroom, while an estimated 770,000 children have experienced psychological distress.

# U.S. News
* **Senate blocks resolution on occupied West Bank:** The United States Senate [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/3e2a6eb0-0514-4d3e-b970-e60cbf438122?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to block a resolution on Tuesday that would have forced the State Department to report on the killings of American citizens by Israeli settlers and soldiers in the occupied West Bank. It would have required a report within 30 days on investigations into the killings of U.S. citizens by settlers or Israeli forces. If the administration failed to deliver the report, most U.S. security assistance to Israel would have been cut off.
* The resolution failed 47-53. Sen. **John Fetterman** of Pennsylvania was the only Democrat to vote against the resolution, while Republican Sen. **Rand Paul** of Kentucky joined Democrats in supporting it.
* Nine American citizens have been killed in the West Bank since 2022, the resolution noted; none of their killers have been held to account by either the Israeli or U.S. government.

* **Supreme Court allows Trump 's third-country deportation policy to resume**: The Supreme Court [granted](https://substack.com/redirect/1abeb39c-b818-4863-b13a-4a8a61465975?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an emergency request Tuesday allowing the Trump administration to resume deporting immigrants to "third countries" where they have no ties. Oral arguments are scheduled for December to issue a definitive ruling.
* The order reverses a 1st Circuit Court of Appeals decision that sided with plaintiffs arguing people deserve a "meaningful opportunity" to raise safety concerns before removal to a third country.
* Roughly 25,000 people were deported to third countries since February of 2025, according to court records.
* **ICE plans to hire 5,000 more officers by year 's end**: ICE is [preparing](https://substack.com/redirect/8c8066f8-9079-41a7-b216-980cb7988dbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to hire 5,000 new employees, according to the New York Times, expanding its workforce by roughly 17% after growing by about 8,000 to reach 29,000 employees since Trump took office.
* Most recruits are expected to become "deportation officers," who conduct arrests and manage deportation cases. Their hiring will draw on the more than $100 billion in new funding granted the agency by Congress.
* During last year's rapid hiring surge, hundreds of recruits were removed after being let in with limited or no initial vetting. One of these recruits, **David Brouillette** , was identified as the agent who fatally shot Colombian immigrant **Johan Sebasti an Duran Guerrero **in Maine in July.
* **California passes law banning shock gloves for law enforcement:** California passed a law banning local, state, and federal law enforcement personnel from using gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks to people.
* ICE awarded a nearly $17 million contract to purchase 6,000 pairs last month. The ban on the gloves will take effect next year and remain in place until 2030.
* **DHS confirms $20 million in taxpayer funds spent on pro-Trump ads, drawing bipartisan criticism** : The Department of Homeland Security [committed](https://substack.com/redirect/877e7d47-34e0-427f-b822-f132cf19cc9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $20 million from Trump's "One Big Beautiful Bill"--funds intended for Customs and Border Protection--to fund campaign-style ads glorifying the president, according to a Tuesday letter from Sens. **Patty Murray** and **Chris Murphy** , who called the ads "a shockingly corrupt misuse of taxpayer dollars" and demanded answers within 48 hours. The ads, which began running last week during NFL and college football broadcasts, have drawn criticism from both parties.
* **Tech executives sign "morally binding" AI accord at White House lunch with Trump**: Tech executives, including Anthropic's **Dario Amodei** , OpenAI's **Greg Brockman** , Meta's **Mark Zuckerberg** , Nvidia's **Jensen Huang** , and **Elon Musk** , [signed](https://substack.com/redirect/e696c08b-5365-4498-883b-54796ad22a8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a "morally binding" constitution on AI governance during a White House lunch Tuesday. At the meeting, Trump also floated forming a 10-person oversight committee for the industry.
* President Donald Trump claimed that the tech leaders showed evidence of "tremendous self-policing," and that they assured him they were putting the "appropriate guardrails" on their models, which have been the subject of recent hacking controversies in the U.S. and Australia.
* Zuckerberg told reporters that the Tuesday framework centers on companies maintaining "robust internal controls," including internal risk reviews and third-party audits reviewed by company boards, calling it "a start and an accord that the whole industry could come to."
* **IRS to add citizenship question to tax forms:** The IRS is [preparing](https://substack.com/redirect/1a2d08ab-f9a4-4227-9e0e-8a68d6909815?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to add a citizenship and work-authorization question to next year's Form 1040, though tax experts say the change serves no clear administrative purpose since existing tax benefits already require valid Social Security numbers.
* "The only reason you have that attestation is to deter people," a former IRS official told the New York Times when asked about the policy change.
* **Trump administration preparing to auto-enroll all children in Trump Accounts before midterms:** The government is [preparing](https://substack.com/redirect/3f1d66ff-2688-4b2e-803f-20ed8c2d9dd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to use IRS data to automatically enroll all children under 18 in tax-advantaged "Trump Accounts," aiming to reach up to 60 million additional children weeks before the midterms. Only 5% of eligible middle- and lower-income families had voluntarily enrolled by summer, sources told The Washington Sun.
* It is unclear what advantages would accrue to those enrolled, given that most families remain ineligible for the program's flagship $1,000 benefit for babies born 2025-2028.
* **Trump 's ban on $1 billion in Canadian imports takes effect**: President Trump's ban on nearly $1 billion worth of Canadian goods, including dairy products, motor vehicles, and alcohol, [took effect](https://substack.com/redirect/16e7258f-ad24-4e82-8755-07adfd9c40f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday, the latest escalation in an ongoing trade war.
* **Federal prosecutors charge Wilber Garces Perez with assaulting ICE officer in Austin shooting** : Federal prosecutors in Texas [charged](https://substack.com/redirect/9c1f732a-ee11-4a66-b0af-53ba8b7628a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Wilber Rafael Garces Perez** , the Venezuelan delivery driver shot by an ICE agent in Austin, with assaulting a federal officer, alleging in an eight-page affidavit that his car's side-view mirror struck agent "L.G." as he drove away to evade arrest.
* The affidavit, based on an interview with another agent whose body camera captured the incident and Garces Perez himself, describes a short pursuit that ended when an SUV struck his car, after which Garces Perez said L.G. fired his pistol through the back-right window, striking him in the upper back. That bullet remains lodged near his spine and had not been removed as of last week. L.G., who was not wearing a body camera, gave no account in the filing.
* **Senate GOP leaves Trump 's $350 billion defense funding request in limbo before recess:** Senate Republicans are [set to leave](https://substack.com/redirect/fb493f46-2087-4acd-af90-64b424e77ec0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Washington for recess without approving President Trump's $350 billion defense reconciliation request, part of a broader push toward a $1.5 trillion total defense budget, as party members remain divided over financing.
* Defense hawks, including Sen. **Kevin Cramer**(N.D.), want the full amount to fund priorities including the Golden Dome missile shield. Deficit hawks like Sen. **Ron Johnson**(Wis.), chair of the Budget Committee, have objected, with Johnson saying he won't move a reconciliation package until after the midterms without identified spending offsets.
* Pentagon Comptroller **Jay Hurst** said Congress may incorporate some priorities, particularly munitions investments, into the regular discretionary budget instead, though that process is also stalled, with government funding only secured through December 11.

# Other International News
* **Commercial plane traveling from UAE to Israel forced to land in Saudi Arabia after fight between pilots:** A fight between pilots on a commercial FlyDubai flight from the United Arab Emirates to Israel forced the aircraft to make a dramatic emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday.
* Around two and a half hours after departing from Dubai on its way to Tel Aviv, the plane descended from 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet within a minute, before turning close to the Jordanian border and eventually landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.
* An Israeli official told the AP a fight broke out between two pilots, one of whom was armed with a knife. It wasn't immediately clear what caused the fight. The aircraft's captain and the first officer were injured and taken to the hospital upon landing.
* During the incident, Israel scrambled warplanes, fearing a hijacking of a plane. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement that Saudi Arabia had arrested the pilot who allegedly stabbed the other one. Netanyahu claimed passengers and crew members on the flight managed to subdue the pilot, preventing a "major disaster."
* **Scandal rocks Fl avio Bolsonaro campaign ahead of first round election in Brazil:** Right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro faces a new corruption scandal days ahead of the October 4 election following a report [published](https://substack.com/redirect/05b5ccf9-0fa8-4df8-851e-ce5e068fa96e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Brazilian outlet PlatoBR. Leaked messages, photos, and financial records from disgruntled former business partner Alexandre Santini link Bolsonaro to lavish gifts, including a $60,000 Rolex, sex parties allegedly paid for with suspect funds, and an attempt to lobby a Supreme Court justice.
* A fresh AtlasIntel poll shows President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva leading 45.3% to 42.2%.
* **Amnesty: Mali army, Wagner mercenaries killed at least 34 civilians in seven incidents** : An Amnesty International report [accuses](https://substack.com/redirect/4f0b9d3b-0cdd-4f80-b70b-404f827ecb96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) forces from Russia's Wagner Group and the Malian army of killing at least 34 civilians across Mali's Segou, Mopti, and Timbuktu regions, in seven incidents between June 2023 and December 2025.
* The victims, according to the report, were mostly pastoralist community members targeted based on their ethnicity or killed because they lived in areas with active jihadist groups.
* Describing the incidents as war crimes and "deliberate," the report noted that "victims were shot, had their throats cut, or were burned alive." It also provided accounts of torture by Wagner members during patrols and detentions.
* **UN renews Haiti security force mandate:** The UN Security Council [extended](https://substack.com/redirect/b31e1b2e-ebd0-4511-b2f8-38b34787d0f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Gang Suppression Force's mandate in Haiti by six months to March 31, 2027. Twelve member states voted in favor of the extension, though China, Russia, and Pakistan abstained over concerns about insufficient funding, personnel and efficacy.
* The force, meant to provide security ahead of Haiti's Dec. 13 elections, is currently deployed at less than 30 percent of its intended size.
* **Russian strikes kill four, including a child, in Kyiv region overnight** : Russian air strikes [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/7847e230-d2d1-4f39-9495-e9974ee43d60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four people, including a child, and injured seven more in and around Kyiv early Wednesday, with Kyiv City Military Administration reporting two dead and four injured in the capital itself.
* Neighboring NATO members Romania and Poland scrambled military jets to protect their airspace amid the attacks.
* Separately, a Ukrainian drone strike damaged private houses in Russia's Samara region, an oil-producing hub roughly 1,100 kilometers southeast of Moscow.
* **Belgium to transfer three F-16s to Ukraine by year 's end, Zelenskyy says**: Belgium agreed to transfer three F-16 fighter jets to Ukraine by the end of the year, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy [said](https://substack.com/redirect/35df4bf7-5e27-46d9-bcdc-70ddad2b18fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), noting that Ukraine has already received urgent F-16 ammunition deliveries from Belgium and Spain.
* **Russian Tu-95 bomber crashes during training, killing six crew:** A Russian nuclear-capable Tu-95 strategic bomber [crashed](https://substack.com/redirect/33493b03-01cd-49fd-861f-4f121f8a971e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday during a training mission in the country's far east, killing six crew members, with one survivor hospitalized, Russia's Defense Ministry said.
* The unarmed aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the village of Krasnoyarovo on the Zeya River, close to the Chinese border, with regional officials saying the pilots "did all they could to steer the plane away from residential buildings."
* **Lithuania offers to pay for permanent U.S. troop presence, PM says** : Lithuania "ready to pay the bill" for a permanent U.S. military base, its prime minister told Bloomberg TV: "We would definitely go for it if they're ready, and we would ensure the best possible conditions for the troops."
* The push comes as Trump separately announced "major progress" last week toward establishing a permanent base in neighboring Poland--which President Karol Nawrocki suggested calling "Fort Trump."
* Lithuania, located about 67 miles from mainland Russia, prepares to hold the EU's rotating presidency in early 2027.
* **UN says North Korea violated armistice; North Korea dismisses DMZ mine blast findings as "farce":** On Wednesday, North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, [called](https://substack.com/redirect/7563a687-cd98-40d9-9d6e-f4c9c38190c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a South Korean investigation into last week's DMZ mine blast "low and dirty" and a "farce," accusing Seoul of fabricating evidence. South Korean Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul said North Korean mines caused the explosion that wounded three South Korean soldiers and warned of "corresponding" action.
* The UN Command, which oversees the Korean armistice, found another active North Korean anti-personnel mine during a joint on-site investigation with South Korean authorities on Wednesday, and determined "an Armistice Agreement violation occurred."
* **Afghanistan says it killed 41, captured 62 insurgents crossing from Pakistan in three days:** Afghanistan's defense ministry [said](https://substack.com/redirect/11590e19-fb66-4c9a-827b-88a04347df00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday its forces killed 41 alleged insurgents and captured 62 more over three days this week, claiming the fighters crossed from Pakistan "with the support" of Islamabad and that the group included members of the Islamic State group. Pakistan did not immediately comment, though it has rejected similar claims.
* **Somali pirates kill five crew members before tanker rescue by Puntland forces** : Somali pirates [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/0d491a18-edae-4441-8969-7624b62575de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) five crew members--three Pakistanis, one Myanmar national, and one Indian national--aboard the hijacked tanker MT Honour 25 before Puntland security forces rescued the ship and captured 16 pirates, Puntland's information ministry said Tuesday, marking the apparent first deaths at the hands of Somali pirates in over a decade.
* Drop Site contributor Mohamed Gabobe reports on the seizure of the Honour and another vessel, the MT Eureka, in a piece published Tuesday. **Gabobe 's report is available in full [here](https://substack.com/redirect/0d491a18-edae-4441-8969-7624b62575de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Fighting between SPLM-N, Otoro tribe kills over 500 in Sudan 's Nuba Mountains: **More than 500 people from the Otoro ethnic group have been [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/e9b1f24f-b1bc-4e99-be4b-8e3ce8c71a99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and over 25,000 displaced in months of fighting around Kauda in Sudan's South Kordofan/Nuba Mountains region, Otoro acting chief Koko al-Degeil Damgala told Sudan Tribune on Wednesday. Fatalities continue to mount daily, he said, while displaced residents are sheltering in caves without humanitarian aid.
* Damgala rejected accusations that the Otoro rebelled against the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N), saying that the tribe remained invested in the group's political project, but that it had recently rebelled against "systemic marginalization and misrule" in the region. He claimed that the SPLM-N had begun a wave of arbitrary detentions of prominent Otoro in April, sweeping up aid workers, civil servants, military personnel, and local traders.
* **Malaysia begins sending nearly 1,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar despite safety concerns** : Malaysia [began](https://substack.com/redirect/19b24326-1a16-4961-8597-9ece1f78e720?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) transporting nearly 1,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar Tuesday under police escort, describing the returns as "voluntary" despite UN warnings that "conditions for safe and dignified returns" to Myanmar do not exist for the Rohingya.
* Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim reached an agreement with Myanmar's military government in July to return 5,000 refugees; the 1,500 returned on Tuesday are part of this group. Doctors Without Borders and more than 160 civil society organizations called for the returns to be halted.
* **300,000 join French civil servant strikes; student protests turn violent nationwide:** Roughly 300,000 civil servants, including teachers, firefighters, and healthcare workers, [joined](https://substack.com/redirect/e0a059d6-087f-430e-a15b-19153376e804?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a one-day nationwide strike Tuesday demanding higher pay and better conditions, with police estimating 30,000 marched in Paris. Separate student protests over school conditions turned violent, injuring 10 students and staff and 48 law enforcement officials, with 440 people detained.
* General Confederation of Labor general secretary Sophie Binet called the demonstrations "a red alert," giving the government 48 hours to reverse planned budget cuts, including a proposed annual salary freeze for state workers.
* **UK 's Burnham vows sweeping public service expansion in first conference speech as PM: **British Prime Minister Andy Burnham [used](https://substack.com/redirect/b5b232e8-85e1-4d74-a797-19c085fbf98e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his first Labour conference speech Tuesday to promise a "new path" for Britain, pledging to create a "National Care Service," "free...at the point of use" to give UK residents access to state-funded caregivers, to make adjustments to the "pension triple lock" (which sets the rate by which pensions are raised) by April 2030, and to reduce deposit requirements for young homebuyers.
* He also promised drastic changes to British utility provisions, saying he would reverse a Thatcher-era "ban on public ownership of water companies," and that his government would seek to create a new publicly owned "Great British Grid" to challenge private electricity operators.
* Regarding Britain's foreign relations, Burnham pledged to "stand up to" Russian and Iranian threats and continue its "principled leadership" in support of a two-state solution for Israel and Palestine.

Drop Site Daily: September 30, 2026 | | | Sep 30 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- A Flydubai plane is parked on the Apron of Ben Gurion International Airport. Photo by Jamal Awad/picture alliance via Getty Images. Wednesday, September 30, 2026 -** Iran : Iran says it received U.S. response to Strait of Hormuz proposal. U.S. sanctions ten entities in China, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia over Iran arms procurement. U.S. offers 40 million barrels from strategic reserve. Qatari Prime Minister says Iran war pushed country into budget deficit. Three tankers struck by unknown projectiles in Strait of Hormuz. No explosives found in vans near RAF Fairford, UK police say. Iran executes two more over January protests. Yemen : UAE vice president visits Saudi Arabia for first time since rift. Ansarallah ballistic missiles strike Saudi-backed forces' camps in southern Yemen. Palestine : Israeli strike on vehicle kills six in Gaza City as death toll since Tuesday reaches 13. Israeli forces raid homes, settlers attack Palestinian property across the occupied West Bank. Gaza child mortality more than doubled in 2025 amid Israeli attacks. Qatar PM: Hamas agreed to release all civilian hostages on October 7. Lebanon : Lebanese soldier, civilians wounded in Nabatieh as Israeli ceasefire violations continue across the south. Four in five Lebanese households struggle to afford basic needs as conflict deepens crisis. U.S. : Senate blocks resolution on occupied West Bank. Supreme Court allows President Donald Trump's third-country deportation policy to resume. ICE plans to hire 5,000 more officers by year's end. California passes law banning shock gloves for law enforcement. Tech executives sign "morally binding" AI accord at White House lunch with Trump. DHS confirms $20 million in taxpayer funds spent on pro-Trump ads, drawing bipartisan criticism. IRS to add citizenship question to tax forms. Trump administration preparing to auto-enroll all children in Trump Accounts before midterms. Trump's ban on $1 billion in Canadian imports takes effect. Federal prosecutors charge Wilber Garces Perez with assaulting ICE officer in Austin shooting. Senate GOP leaves Trump's $350 billion defense funding request in limbo before recess. International : Commercial plane traveling from UAE to Israel forced to land in Saudi Arabia after fight between pilots. Scandal rocks Flavio Bolsonaro campaign ahead of first-round election in Brazil. Amnesty: Mali army, Wagner mercenaries killed at least 34 civilians in seven incidents. UN renews Haiti security force mandate. Belgium to transfer three F-16s to Ukraine by year's end, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says. Russian Tu-95 bomber crashes during training, killing six crew. Lithuania offers to pay for permanent US troop presence, PM says. UN says North Korea violated armistice; North Korea dismisses DMZ mine blast findings as "farce." Afghanistan says it killed 41, captured 62 insurgents crossing from Pakistan in three days. Somali pirates kill five crew members before tanker rescue by Puntland forces. Fighting between SPLM-N, Otoro tribe kills over 500 in Sudan's Nuba Mountains. Malaysia begins sending nearly 1,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar despite safety concerns. 300,000 join French civil servant strikes; student protests turn violent nationwide. UK's Burnham vows sweeping public service expansion in first conference speech as PM. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iran says it received U.S. response to Hormuz proposal: Iran a U.S. proposal amid indirect talks over reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a government spokesperson said, without disclosing details. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented the proposal to President Masoud Pezeshkian during a cabinet meeting after briefing officials on his meetings in New York, Mohajerani said. U.S. sanctions ten entities in China, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia over Iran arms procurement : The Treasury Department sanctioned ten individuals and companies, including representatives and technology firms based in China, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia (and three based in Iran), accusing them of procuring weapons and parts for Iran's Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics. The sanctions targeted Hong Kong-based EC Mojo Technology Co Ltd, which the U.S. has accused of supplying electronic components and evading export controls. The U.S. also sanctioned the Saudi-based Cavalier Dynamics for Technologies Company. U.S. offers 40 million barrels from strategic reserve: The Trump administration to lend up to 40 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve on Tuesday, as fuel prices remain near record highs seven months into the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The barrels are the last tranche of the 172 million the U.S. pledged in March to an International Energy Agency release of 400 million barrels coordinated among about 30 countries. The release is structured as an exchange, not a sale: companies borrow the oil and later return it with additional barrels as a premium. Bids are due on October 6. The reserve held 283.8 million barrels as of September 25, its lowest level in 44 years, according to Energy Department data. Qatar PM says Iran war pushed country into budget deficit: Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani the war on Iran one of the biggest crises in Qatar's history, telling Piers Morgan that LNG exports through Hormuz are "barely happening." He was asked about a reported $24 billion in lost gas sales, an IMF forecast of more than 8% contraction this year, an 80% drop in visitors and hotels 60% empty, and said "many of those numbers" were accurate. He said after an Iranian missile hit Qatar's LNG facility the country now faces a budget deficit. It has cut secondary projects but not salaries, leaning on its sovereign wealth fund. "It's not a structural contraction for our economy," he clarified, saying LNG output will return once damaged trains are repaired. Three tankers struck by unknown projectiles in Strait of Hormuz: Three tankers were struck by projectiles of unknown origin while transiting the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours, according to incident reports from the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO). One of the crude oil tankers was hit while transiting inbound. No explosives found in vans near RAF Fairford, UK police say: No explosive devices were found in three vans linked to five men arrested near RAF Fairford, the British airbase used by U.S. forces for strikes on Iran, UK counterterrorism police said. Police said a quantity of petrol was recovered and the investigation remains ongoing. The five British nationals were arrested Sunday on suspicion of terrorism before being released on bail Monday. U.S. President Donald Trump criticized the suspects' release and suggested they "might be" connected to Iran. Iran has denied involvement, and UK authorities have not publicly established a foreign link. Iran executes two more over January protests: Iran executed two men on Wednesday on charges related to violence during nationwide anti-government protests in January, according to state news. The men took part in protests in the northeastern city of Mashhad that left four security officers dead and confessed to setting fires, the judiciary determined, damaging public property, and stabbing a member of Iran's paramilitary force. Iran has executed dozens of people on charges related to the January protests in what Amnesty International has followed "torture-tainted grossly unfair trials by Revolutionary Courts." Yemen UAE vice president visits Saudi Arabia for first time since rift : UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan Saudi Arabia Tuesday and met with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, the first senior UAE official to visit the kingdom since a rift emerged last December. It remains unclear whether Saudi Arabia's push for international support against Ansarallah extends to reengaging the UAE, once its main partner in the Yemen war. The two countries' tensions emerged after UAE-backed southern Yemeni separatists advanced near Saudi borders, prompting a Saudi airstrike on a UAE-linked weapons shipment at Mukalla port. The UAE subsequently announced a full withdrawal of its forces from Yemen. Ansarallah ballistic missiles strike Saudi-backed forces ' camps in southern Yemen: Nearly 20 soldiers and officers are believed to be among the dead and wounded, according to OSINT reports, after an Ansarallah ballistic missile a Saudi-backed Homeland Shield Forces military camp in the Al-Qawah area on the southern Yemeni coast on Tuesday. Three ballistic missiles also struck the camp of the Fourth Mountain Infantry Brigade, south of Al-Turbah. Saudi-backed forces claimed to have carried out 414 strikes targeting Ansarallah positions over the past 24 hours, according to the armed forces spokesperson. Palestine Israeli strike on vehicle kills six in Gaza City as death toll since Tuesday reaches 13: Six Palestinians were killed and 15 others wounded on Wednesday when an Israeli hit a vehicle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City, according to WAFA. A woman was killed in an Israeli strike on an apartment near Al-Shifa Medical Complex. Four Palestinians, including two children, were wounded when an Israeli drone struck a tent sheltering displaced people west of Khan Younis, while two others were critically wounded by Israeli gunfire southeast of Deir al-Balah. At least 13 Palestinians have been killed and 42 wounded in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip since Tuesday. Israeli forces raid homes, settlers attack Palestinian property across the occupied West Bank: Tulkarm: Israeli forces widespread raids across the governorate, storming homes in Kafr Zibad, Kafr Jammal, Kafr Abbush, Kafr Sur, Far'un, Attil, Deir Al-Ghusun, Shuweika, and several neighborhoods of Tulkarm city on Wednesday, WAFA reported. Forces converted some homes into military posts, set up checkpoints and detained several Palestinians, including former prisoners. Jenin: Israeli forces families out of homes in Jenin's Old City and Marah Saad and converted several buildings into military posts. Forces were deployed across the city and along the Jenin-Nablus road and closed iron gates at entrances to nearby towns and villages. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: In Taybeh, settlers a family home, beating family members and spraying them with pepper spray, injuring a teenage boy. Bethlehem: Settlers a drinking-water pipeline supplying a Bedouin community of around 800 Palestinians in Al-Rashaydeh, southeast of Bethlehem. Nablus: Israeli forces several neighborhoods of Nablus and the town of Deir Sharaf, firing stun grenades and tear gas. An 80-year-old man was hospitalized after soldiers beat him, while Palestinians were detained, including three 14-year-old boys in Deir Sharaf. Gaza child mortality more than doubled in 2025 amid Israeli attacks: The mortality rate for children under five in Gaza more than doubled to 33.4 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2025, up from 13.6 in 2022, according to the Health Ministry's first official mortality report since 2022. The ministry estimates the rate would be 15.8 without deaths caused by the war. Israel's direct attacks were the leading cause of death in Gaza in 2025, accounting for 70.1% of the 24,650 recorded deaths. Qatar PM: Hamas agreed to release all civilian hostages on October 7: Hamas on the first day of the war on Gaza to "release all civilian hostages," asking only for a ceasefire window to get them out, and Israel refused to even "entertain the idea," Qatar's Prime Minister confirmed. "We got an agreement" to release "all the civilian hostages," Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani told Piers Morgan. Israeli officials replied that if Hamas wanted to free them, it should do so without a pause in fighting, he said. His on-record account follows a Haaretz report this month that he relayed the offer to then-Mossad chief David Barnea on the evening of October 7. Lebanon Lebanese soldier, civilians wounded in Nabatieh as Israeli ceasefire violations continue across south: A Lebanese soldier and at least three civilians were wounded in an explosion in Nabatieh Al-Fawqa on Wednesday. Elsewhere in southern Lebanon, an Israeli Merkava tank two shells toward a home in Bra'shit early Wednesday, the state's National News Agency reported. Israeli artillery also struck Haddatha, Kfar Tebnit, Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah, Bra'shit, and Wadi Al-Salouqi overnight, while Israeli forces carried out two explosions near Beit Yahoun and Aita Al-Jabal. Four in five Lebanese households struggle to afford basic needs as conflict deepens crisis: Four in five households in Lebanon are struggling to afford basic necessities, with 22% reporting their children had gone to bed hungry in the previous two weeks and 14% reporting at least one child working, according to a new UNICEF . Since March 2, at least 261 children have been killed and 1,056 injured in Israeli attacks, averaging seven children killed or wounded each day over six months, UNICEF said. Some 436 schools have been damaged or destroyed, putting around 100,000 children at risk of being without a classroom, while an estimated 770,000 children have experienced psychological distress. U.S. News Senate blocks resolution on occupied West Bank: The United States Senate to block a resolution on Tuesday that would have forced the State Department to report on the killings of American citizens by Israeli settlers and soldiers in the occupied West Bank. It would have required a report within 30 days on investigations into the killings of U.S. citizens by settlers or Israeli forces. If the administration failed to deliver the report, most U.S. security assistance to Israel would have been cut off. The resolution failed 47-53. Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania was the only Democrat to vote against the resolution, while Republican Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky joined Democrats in supporting it. Nine American citizens have been killed in the West Bank since 2022, the resolution noted; none of their killers have been held to account by either the Israeli or U.S. government. Supreme Court allows Trump 's third-country deportation policy to resume: The Supreme Court an emergency request Tuesday allowing the Trump administration to resume deporting immigrants to "third countries" where they have no ties. Oral arguments are scheduled for December to issue a definitive ruling. The order reverses a 1st Circuit Court of Appeals decision that sided with plaintiffs arguing people deserve a "meaningful opportunity" to raise safety concerns before removal to a third country. Roughly 25,000 people were deported to third countries since February of 2025, according to court records. ICE plans to hire 5,000 more officers by year 's end: ICE is to hire 5,000 new employees, according to the New York Times, expanding its workforce by roughly 17% after growing by about 8,000 to reach 29,000 employees since Trump took office. Most recruits are expected to become "deportation officers," who conduct arrests and manage deportation cases. Their hiring will draw on the more than $100 billion in new funding granted the agency by Congress. During last year's rapid hiring surge, hundreds of recruits were removed after being let in with limited or no initial vetting. One of these recruits, David Brouillette , was identified as the agent who fatally shot Colombian immigrant Johan Sebasti an Duran Guerrero in Maine in July. California passes law banning shock gloves for law enforcement: California passed a law banning local, state, and federal law enforcement personnel from using gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks to people. ICE awarded a nearly $17 million contract to purchase 6,000 pairs last month. The ban on the gloves will take effect next year and remain in place until 2030. DHS confirms $20 million in taxpayer funds spent on pro-Trump ads, drawing bipartisan criticism : The Department of Homeland Security $20 million from Trump's "One Big Beautiful Bill"--funds intended for Customs and Border Protection--to fund campaign-style ads glorifying the president, according to a Tuesday letter from Sens. Patty Murray and Chris Murphy , who called the ads "a shockingly corrupt misuse of taxpayer dollars" and demanded answers within 48 hours. The ads, which began running last week during NFL and college football broadcasts, have drawn criticism from both parties. Tech executives sign "morally binding" AI accord at White House lunch with Trump: Tech executives, including Anthropic's Dario Amodei , OpenAI's Greg Brockman , Meta's Mark Zuckerberg , Nvidia's Jensen Huang , and Elon Musk , a "morally binding" constitution on AI governance during a White House lunch Tuesday. At the meeting, Trump also floated forming a 10-person oversight committee for the industry. President Donald Trump claimed that the tech leaders showed evidence of "tremendous self-policing," and that they assured him they were putting the "appropriate guardrails" on their models, which have been the subject of recent hacking controversies in the U.S. and Australia. Zuckerberg told reporters that the Tuesday framework centers on companies maintaining "robust internal controls," including internal risk reviews and third-party audits reviewed by company boards, calling it "a start and an accord that the whole industry could come to." IRS to add citizenship question to tax forms: The IRS is to add a citizenship and work-authorization question to next year's Form 1040, though tax experts say the change serves no clear administrative purpose since existing tax benefits already require valid Social Security numbers. "The only reason you have that attestation is to deter people," a former IRS official told the New York Times when asked about the policy change. Trump administration preparing to auto-enroll all children in Trump Accounts before midterms: The government is to use IRS data to automatically enroll all children under 18 in tax-advantaged "Trump Accounts," aiming to reach up to 60 million additional children weeks before the midterms. Only 5% of eligible middle- and lower-income families had voluntarily enrolled by summer, sources told The Washington Sun. It is unclear what advantages would accrue to those enrolled, given that most families remain ineligible for the program's flagship $1,000 benefit for babies born 2025-2028. Trump 's ban on $1 billion in Canadian imports takes effect: President Trump's ban on nearly $1 billion worth of Canadian goods, including dairy products, motor vehicles, and alcohol, Tuesday, the latest escalation in an ongoing trade war. Federal prosecutors charge Wilber Garces Perez with assaulting ICE officer in Austin shooting : Federal prosecutors in Texas Wilber Rafael Garces Perez , the Venezuelan delivery driver shot by an ICE agent in Austin, with assaulting a federal officer, alleging in an eight-page affidavit that his car's side-view mirror struck agent "L.G." as he drove away to evade arrest. The affidavit, based on an interview with another agent whose body camera captured the incident and Garces Perez himself, describes a short pursuit that ended when an SUV struck his car, after which Garces Perez said L.G. fired his pistol through the back-right window, striking him in the upper back. That bullet remains lodged near his spine and had not been removed as of last week. L.G., who was not wearing a body camera, gave no account in the filing. Senate GOP leaves Trump 's $350 billion defense funding request in limbo before recess: Senate Republicans are Washington for recess without approving President Trump's $350 billion defense reconciliation request, part of a broader push toward a $1.5 trillion total defense budget, as party members remain divided over financing. Defense hawks, including Sen. Kevin Cramer(N.D.), want the full amount to fund priorities including the Golden Dome missile shield. Deficit hawks like Sen. Ron Johnson(Wis.), chair of the Budget Committee, have objected, with Johnson saying he won't move a reconciliation package until after the midterms without identified spending offsets. Pentagon Comptroller Jay Hurst said Congress may incorporate some priorities, particularly munitions investments, into the regular discretionary budget instead, though that process is also stalled, with government funding only secured through December 11. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Commercial plane traveling from UAE to Israel forced to land in Saudi Arabia after fight between pilots: A fight between pilots on a commercial FlyDubai flight from the United Arab Emirates to Israel forced the aircraft to make a dramatic emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday. Around two and a half hours after departing from Dubai on its way to Tel Aviv, the plane descended from 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet within a minute, before turning close to the Jordanian border and eventually landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. An Israeli official told the AP a fight broke out between two pilots, one of whom was armed with a knife. It wasn't immediately clear what caused the fight. The aircraft's captain and the first officer were injured and taken to the hospital upon landing. During the incident, Israel scrambled warplanes, fearing a hijacking of a plane. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement that Saudi Arabia had arrested the pilot who allegedly stabbed the other one. Netanyahu claimed passengers and crew members on the flight managed to subdue the pilot, preventing a "major disaster." Scandal rocks Fl avio Bolsonaro campaign ahead of first round election in Brazil: Right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro faces a new corruption scandal days ahead of the October 4 election following a report by Brazilian outlet PlatoBR. Leaked messages, photos, and financial records from disgruntled former business partner Alexandre Santini link Bolsonaro to lavish gifts, including a $60,000 Rolex, sex parties allegedly paid for with suspect funds, and an attempt to lobby a Supreme Court justice. A fresh AtlasIntel poll shows President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva leading 45.3% to 42.2%. Amnesty: Mali army, Wagner mercenaries killed at least 34 civilians in seven incidents : An Amnesty International report forces from Russia's Wagner Group and the Malian army of killing at least 34 civilians across Mali's Segou, Mopti, and Timbuktu regions, in seven incidents between June 2023 and December 2025. The victims, according to the report, were mostly pastoralist community members targeted based on their ethnicity or killed because they lived in areas with active jihadist groups. Describing the incidents as war crimes and "deliberate," the report noted that "victims were shot, had their throats cut, or were burned alive." It also provided accounts of torture by Wagner members during patrols and detentions. UN renews Haiti security force mandate: The UN Security Council the Gang Suppression Force's mandate in Haiti by six months to March 31, 2027. Twelve member states voted in favor of the extension, though China, Russia, and Pakistan abstained over concerns about insufficient funding, personnel and efficacy. The force, meant to provide security ahead of Haiti's Dec. 13 elections, is currently deployed at less than 30 percent of its intended size. Russian strikes kill four, including a child, in Kyiv region overnight : Russian air strikes four people, including a child, and injured seven more in and around Kyiv early Wednesday, with Kyiv City Military Administration reporting two dead and four injured in the capital itself. Neighboring NATO members Romania and Poland scrambled military jets to protect their airspace amid the attacks. Separately, a Ukrainian drone strike damaged private houses in Russia's Samara region, an oil-producing hub roughly 1,100 kilometers southeast of Moscow. Belgium to transfer three F-16s to Ukraine by year 's end, Zelenskyy says: Belgium agreed to transfer three F-16 fighter jets to Ukraine by the end of the year, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , noting that Ukraine has already received urgent F-16 ammunition deliveries from Belgium and Spain. Russian Tu-95 bomber crashes during training, killing six crew: A Russian nuclear-capable Tu-95 strategic bomber Tuesday during a training mission in the country's far east, killing six crew members, with one survivor hospitalized, Russia's Defense Ministry said. The unarmed aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the village of Krasnoyarovo on the Zeya River, close to the Chinese border, with regional officials saying the pilots "did all they could to steer the plane away from residential buildings." Lithuania offers to pay for permanent U.S. troop presence, PM says : Lithuania "ready to pay the bill" for a permanent U.S. military base, its prime minister told Bloomberg TV: "We would definitely go for it if they're ready, and we would ensure the best possible conditions for the troops." The push comes as Trump separately announced "major progress" last week toward establishing a permanent base in neighboring Poland--which President Karol Nawrocki suggested calling "Fort Trump." Lithuania, located about 67 miles from mainland Russia, prepares to hold the EU's rotating presidency in early 2027. UN says North Korea violated armistice; North Korea dismisses DMZ mine blast findings as "farce": On Wednesday, North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, a South Korean investigation into last week's DMZ mine blast "low and dirty" and a "farce," accusing Seoul of fabricating evidence. South Korean Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul said North Korean mines caused the explosion that wounded three South Korean soldiers and warned of "corresponding" action. The UN Command, which oversees the Korean armistice, found another active North Korean anti-personnel mine during a joint on-site investigation with South Korean authorities on Wednesday, and determined "an Armistice Agreement violation occurred." Afghanistan says it killed 41, captured 62 insurgents crossing from Pakistan in three days: Afghanistan's defense ministry on Wednesday its forces killed 41 alleged insurgents and captured 62 more over three days this week, claiming the fighters crossed from Pakistan "with the support" of Islamabad and that the group included members of the Islamic State group. Pakistan did not immediately comment, though it has rejected similar claims. Somali pirates kill five crew members before tanker rescue by Puntland forces : Somali pirates five crew members--three Pakistanis, one Myanmar national, and one Indian national--aboard the hijacked tanker MT Honour 25 before Puntland security forces rescued the ship and captured 16 pirates, Puntland's information ministry said Tuesday, marking the apparent first deaths at the hands of Somali pirates in over a decade. Drop Site contributor Mohamed Gabobe reports on the seizure of the Honour and another vessel, the MT Eureka, in a piece published Tuesday. Gabobe 's report is available in full . Fighting between SPLM-N, Otoro tribe kills over 500 in Sudan 's Nuba Mountains: More than 500 people from the Otoro ethnic group have been and over 25,000 displaced in months of fighting around Kauda in Sudan's South Kordofan/Nuba Mountains region, Otoro acting chief Koko al-Degeil Damgala told Sudan Tribune on Wednesday. Fatalities continue to mount daily, he said, while displaced residents are sheltering in caves without humanitarian aid. Damgala rejected accusations that the Otoro rebelled against the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N), saying that the tribe remained invested in the group's political project, but that it had recently rebelled against "systemic marginalization and misrule" in the region. He claimed that the SPLM-N had begun a wave of arbitrary detentions of prominent Otoro in April, sweeping up aid workers, civil servants, military personnel, and local traders. Malaysia begins sending nearly 1,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar despite safety concerns : Malaysia transporting nearly 1,500 Rohingya refugees back to Myanmar Tuesday under police escort, describing the returns as "voluntary" despite UN warnings that "conditions for safe and dignified returns" to Myanmar do not exist for the Rohingya. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim reached an agreement with Myanmar's military government in July to return 5,000 refugees; the 1,500 returned on Tuesday are part of this group. Doctors Without Borders and more than 160 civil society organizations called for the returns to be halted. 300,000 join French civil servant strikes; student protests turn violent nationwide: Roughly 300,000 civil servants, including teachers, firefighters, and healthcare workers, a one-day nationwide strike Tuesday demanding higher pay and better conditions, with police estimating 30,000 marched in Paris. Separate student protests over school conditions turned violent, injuring 10 students and staff and 48 law enforcement officials, with 440 people detained. General Confederation of Labor general secretary Sophie Binet called the demonstrations "a red alert," giving the government 48 hours to reverse planned budget cuts, including a proposed annual salary freeze for state workers. Just this Wednesday I was on the air with Olivia from Tennessee Conservative News talking about how the death penalty doesn't apply to child rape if the child doesn't die -- that's the Supreme Court's rule, and fine, that's the law. But today the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals taught me something new: apparently the death penalty doesn't fully apply to murder either -- not when the method might scare the person being executed.
Because that's the only way to read what happened in Tennessee today. The penalty of death, we are now told, must be administered peacefully. Comfortably. Maybe with a conversation. Light a candle, burn some incense, hand out lilies, I guess -- regardless of how horribly the victim died. Crazy days.
Christa Pike killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in Knoxville in 1995 -- a brutal, senseless murder committed when Pike herself was barely more than a teenager. It is incredibly rare for a woman to be sentenced to death in this country, so you know it was bad if she was going to die. Only 18 women have been executed in the modern death penalty era, which began in 1977. The most recent was Amber McLaughlin in Missouri in 2023 -- unlucky her, I guess, wrong circuit. 8th not 6th. Women account for 1% of all executions; men account for the other 1,664. Experts say that's because women commit fewer violent crimes. Fine.
Researchers have also found that 96% of women on death row were raped, sexually abused as children, or subjected to domestic violence before their arrest. I mention that because Pike's lawyers built a 226-page clemency petition on exactly that -- her age at the time of the crime, and the claim that her trial attorney never told the jury she was a victim of extensive child sexual abuse and multiple rapes.
And so we're clear about what kind of guest of the state we're talking about: while on death row, Pike tried to kill a fellow inmate with a shoelace. Not exactly time served with good behavior.
Now watch the dominoes fall. Less than a week before the execution, the Tennessee Supreme Court denied her request for a stay, finding she "failed to demonstrate a likelihood of success on the merits of her claims." Governor Bill Lee confirmed Monday he would not step in to keep Pike alive past her September 30 execution date. The U.S. Supreme Court denied her final stay request yesterday, September 29. So that should have been it. Last chance. But...
The Sixth Circuit issued a stay this morning, filed just before Pike's execution was scheduled to begin at 10 a.m. Quote the order: "The United States District Court for the Eastern District of Tennessee determined that it did not have jurisdiction over Christa Pike's Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60(b)(6) motion to reopen the judgment denying habeas relief... Therefore, it is ORDERED that execution of the sentence of death upon the movant is STAYED until further order of this court."
Read that again. Nobody ruled that her claims were good. Nobody ruled that she's innocent of the procedural mess. The court simply wasn't sure the lower court was *allowed* to say no -- so until they sort that out, no execution. Her lawyers called it the court "recognizing the serious concerns about Christa's scheduled execution." Mind you, this is the court whose territory is Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and Tennessee -- 16 judges, based in Ohio -- and it found a reason that the Governor of Tennessee (state's rights) and the United States Supreme Court (federal, all nine) both passed on.
The "serious concerns" are the protocol arguments. In a hearing last month, Pike's team argued the state's execution protocols would make her death torturous because of her physical, medical, and psychological conditions, including PTSD. The state's answer: she'd be moved to Riverbend Maximum Security Institution 24 hours before, and the goal was that she'd be observed only by female corrections staff. Keep Riverbend in mind for a second.
Riverbend is where Tony Carruthers was supposed to be executed in May, until medical staff spent over an hour failing to establish IV access and the state gave up -- an attempted execution so botched it prompted a pause from Governor Lee. It's where Anthony Darrell Hines was put to death in August for the 1985 murder of Catherine Jean Jackson Jenkins -- so the machinery demonstrably worked a month ago. And the doctor involved in the Carruthers attempt, Mark Fowler, is the one overseeing Pike's. That's the thread the anti-death-penalty groups pulled, and they found a friendly hearing in the Sixth Circuit to buy her time that a Governor and the U.S. Supreme Court didn't deem worthy. (Very much like the mistrial that jury handed that Clancy woman who killed her kids. The court system is busted.)
Pike's letter from death row: "When my people showed up for me -- they have showed up and showed out! I am humbled beyond words." And this: "Whether my clemency is granted or not, I am at peace. I am not afraid to die. I am only nervous about the process."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dbe5a363-da0b-4a6f-98b1-f940fa1461eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There it is. Nervous about the process. Colleen Slemmer didn't get a process. She got thirty years of her mother waiting for justice.
There are currently 45 women on death row across the country, so at this rate we're going to see this four dozen more times. California has the most, 17 -- though Governor Gavin Newsom has ordered that no executions take place since 2019, so those ladies can relax. New York, 7, and Texas, 6, have executed the most women since 1900. Not a lot.
Slemmer's mother, after the stays started falling: "Maybe now finally we have justice. It may not bring my daughter back, but it might save another person from getting killed because she will do it again."
That was the whole point. Not the candle. Not the incense. Not the lilies. Somewhere tonight, lawyers are racing in front of sixteen judges in Ohio over whether a federal court was allowed to hear a motion -- so that a woman condemned for one of the ugliest murders in Tennessee history doesn't have to be nervous about the process. Her victim didn't even get a stay of the parking lot.

| | Just three days into my first term in Congress, a violent mob attacked the Capitol.

**I didn't go to Congress to fight these partisan wars. That day made it clear to me that part of my job in Washington was going to be speaking up and speaking out when something is wrong.

I was elected to solve problems. To deliver for the people at home in the South Sound. That's exactly what I've done every day since.**

This administration has put the American people at war on many fronts: with each other, with our own institutions, and most recently, in a war with Iran that it can't explain.

I'll say it again: there's no exit strategy. Meanwhile, the economy is in the tank, costs keep climbing, and the President is banning news outlets because he needs a distraction.

I'm not waiting for things to get better on their own. My Fairness for Servicemembers and their Families Act is now law, so military death benefits keep pace with the cost of living. That matters in a district that's home to about 100,000 service members and military families at JBLM.

And I'm pushing Democrats to come out swinging with a 100-day agenda: restore the cuts to Medicare and Medicaid, bring back the ACA tax credits, pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Act and the PRO Act, and end this war.

**Last week, the Seattle Times endorsed me and wrote, “Now, more than ever, a plain-spoken, fearless voice is needed in Congress.” I intend to keep being that voice.**

**But tonight at 11:59 p.m. is the last quarterly FEC deadline of the midterms, and the other side will read my report looking for any sign of weakness. Let's not give them one.**

clean_body: | | Just three days into my first term in Congress, a violent mob attacked the Capitol. I didn't go to Congress to fight these partisan wars. That day made it clear to me that part of my job in Washington was going to be speaking up and speaking out when something is wrong. I was elected to solve problems. To deliver for the people at home in the South Sound. That's exactly what I've done every day since. This administration has put the American people at war on many fronts: with each other, with our own institutions, and most recently, in a war with Iran that it can't explain. I'll say it again: there's no exit strategy. Meanwhile, the economy is in the tank, costs keep climbing, and the President is banning news outlets because he needs a distraction. I'm not waiting for things to get better on their own. My Fairness for Servicemembers and their Families Act is now law, so military death benefits keep pace with the cost of living. That matters in a district that's home to about 100,000 service members and military families at JBLM. And I'm pushing Democrats to come out swinging with a 100-day agenda: restore the cuts to Medicare and Medicaid, bring back the ACA tax credits, pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Act and the PRO Act, and end this war. Last week, the Seattle Times endorsed me and wrote, “Now, more than ever, a plain-spoken, fearless voice is needed in Congress.” I intend to keep being that voice. But tonight at 11:59 p.m. is the last quarterly FEC deadline of the midterms, and the other side will read my report looking for any sign of weakness. name: Tim Walz
subject: Before midnight, let’s have Rachel’s back
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Small Town PAC, [smalltownpac
body:
Let’s show the strength behind our candidates and give them the resources to win.
#
Peter,
Tonight is our last public end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before Election Day, and I’m asking you to stand with our endorsed candidate, Rachel Wallace, before we run out of time.
Rachel grew up in Pottsville, Pennsylvania, where her family has lived for 10 generations. She’s served at the State Department, in the Senate, and in the White House — then moved home when her mom was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.
**Now she’s running for Congress to deliver for the community that raised her.**
**[Will you split a donation between Rachel’s campaign and Small Town PAC before midnight to help us put up strong public numbers and give her the resources to flip this district from red to blue?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260930-rw.zJJafi&amount=5&refcode=em20260930-1159&t=1&akid=1159%2E34582%2EuSJY0s)**
Rachel comes from a family of coal miners, farmers, union workers, and small business owners. She knows what it means to work hard and still feel like Washington isn’t listening.
She’s running to lower the cost of living, fix our health care system, and keep our promises to veterans and farmers. That’s the kind of work people need Congress to do. And Rachel has the experience to get to work on day one.
But with less than five weeks until Election Day, she needs more than our endorsement. She needs the resources to get her message in front of voters and make her case through the finish line.
Republican super PACs and MAGA megadonors are pouring money into these races. When our fundraising numbers go public, they’ll be looking to see whether we can keep up the fight. I want them to see a team that’s ready to see this through.
**Small Town PAC needs to raise $60,000 before midnight to help candidates like Rachel compete and win. Every contribution before tonight’s deadline helps us show that strength and fund the work ahead.**
**[Peter, will you split $5 or whatever works for you between Rachel Wallace and Small Town PAC before midnight? Let’s help Rachel flip this seat, take back the House, and give our communities the representation they deserve.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260930-rw.zJJafi&amount=5&refcode=em20260930-1159&t=2&akid=1159%2E34582%2EuSJY0s)**

I’m grateful,
Tim Walz

She’s served at the State Department, in the Senate, and in the White House — then moved home when her mom was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. Now she’s running for Congress to deliver for the community that raised her. Rachel comes from a family of coal miners, farmers, union workers, and small business owners. She knows what it means to work hard and still feel like Washington isn’t listening. She’s running to lower the cost of living, fix our health care system, and keep our promises to veterans and farmers. That’s the kind of work people need Congress to do. And Rachel has the experience to get to work on day one. But with less than five weeks until Election Day, she needs more than our endorsement. She needs the resources to get her message in front of voters and make her case through the finish line. Republican super PACs and MAGA megadonors are pouring money into these races. When our fundraising numbers go public, they’ll be looking to see whether we can keep up the fight. I want them to see a team that’s ready to see this through. Small Town PAC needs to raise $60,000 before midnight to help candidates like Rachel compete and win. Every contribution before tonight’s deadline helps us show that strength and fund the work ahead. I’m grateful, Tim Walz
